items.author: Decrypt Staff
items.content:
In brief
- The World Bank Group said it will explore using Circle’s USDC and blockchain-based payment rails, alongside Citi’s banking connections, to make its global development-funds disbursement faster, cheaper and more transparent than correspondent banking.
- The effort builds on FundsChain, its blockchain platform already tracking disbursements across 350-plus projects in 96 countries.
- It’s a major institutional validator for stablecoins, fitting a Wall Street-onchain wave, from a $270 million bank stablecoin venture to Deutsche Bank’s crypto custody launch.
The World Bank is turning to stablecoins to modernize how it moves development money, announcing Tuesday it will explore using Circle’s USDC and blockchain-based payment rails to speed up and cut the cost of disbursing funds around the world.
The institution said it will work with Citi and Circle to test how dollar-denominated, regulated stablecoins could operate alongside or improve its existing funds-distribution system, which runs on correspondent banking, the slow and costly network of intermediary banks that routes international payments.
Under the arrangement, Citi would supply its connections to established banking rails while Circle provides the infrastructure to mint and settle funds in USDC.
The logic is that even small efficiency gains, applied across the vast sums the World Bank moves, could free up meaningful resources for development. “This initiative is about exploring ways to make the financial plumbing of development work better for the people who need it most,” said World Bank Group President Ajay Banga, arguing that faster, cheaper money movement means “a health clinic gets built on time, a farmer gets paid before the harvest season ends.”
The effort builds on FundsChain, a World Bank blockchain platform designed to make fund disbursements more traceable. More than 350 projects across 96 countries are already onboarded to its digital ledgers, letting everyone involved in a project see how money is being spent.
The stablecoin exploration would focus initially on an intermediated, interoperable model, limited to borrower countries where digital assets are permitted, with plans to involve other banks over time.
Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire framed development finance as one of the most important applications for his company’s technology, saying money that moves “at the speed of the internet shouldn’t be reserved for the world’s biggest banks and corporations.”
Today, the @WorldBankGroup announced work with @circle and @Citi to bring the benefits of USDC to global funds distribution. A big step towards a more efficient and inclusive financial system.https://t.co/hq436tA5IR
— Jeremy Allaire (@jerallaire) November 17, 2026
Citi’s Shahmir Khaliq said the collaboration would deliver “24/7 capabilities at scale so that critical funds move in real time.”
The move hands the stablecoin industry a powerful institutional validator, and it fits a broader wave of traditional finance embracing the technology.
Wall Street is currently racing to claim the onchain dollar, with Goldman Sachs, Citi and other banks committing roughly $270 million to a joint stablecoin venture, while Deutsche Bank recently went live with crypto custody after a five-year buildout.
For Circle, whose USDC is the second-largest stablecoin, a role in the World Bank’s payment plumbing marks a notable step toward mainstream legitimacy, even as the broader crypto market endures a rough stretch of ETF outflows and falling prices.

items.author: Decrypt Staff
items.content:
In brief
- Bitcoin’s realized losses relative to past-year profits hit levels seen only near past cycle lows, Glassnode said, while leverage was largely flushed out.
- Buyers absorbed about 66,000 BTC between $62,000 and $66,000, but demand remains thin, with ETF outflows reaching about $2.2 billion in November.
- A daily close below $62,000 could send Bitcoin toward $58,500 or $53,700, while reclaiming $74,100 would confirm a bottom is forming, according to Glassnode.
Bitcoin’s latest crash has pushed investors into the kind of loss-taking that has historically shown up near market bottoms.
Realized losses, which investors lock in when they sell coins for less than they paid, have climbed relative to the profits taken over the past year.
That measure now sits at levels seen only near the lows of 2018, 2020, 2022 and early 2023, according to a report published Tuesday by onchain analytics firm Glassnode. It’s the first such reading since then.
BTC price on November 22, 4:59PM UTC
Most of the selling came from recent buyers. Holders of coins less than six months old took losses into early 2026, cashed in gains during the rally into September and October, and are now selling at a loss again, Glassnode said. Leverage has been flushed too, with Nov. 13 and 14 bringing some of the largest long liquidations relative to open interest since 2023.
Bitcoin fell to about $62,000 on Nov. 15 before bouncing, and it traded near $64,970 on Tuesday. More than $2 billion in liquidations over the weekend left traders watching $60,000 as a potential next stop, Decrypt reported. The slide deepened last week as fears of further Federal Reserve rate hikes erased Bitcoin’s summer rally. Rising interest rates generally do not bode well for risk assets like Bitcoin, since investors typically rotate to safer bets like U.S. Treasuries when rates elevate.
But there are early signs of support, according to Glassnode. Buyers absorbed about 66,000 BTC in the $62,000 to $66,000 range during the two days of heaviest selling, adding to a zone where recent buyers accumulated around the August low.
Resting bids on Binance and Coinbase within 5% of the price now outweigh asks by about 2.3 to 1. The Coinbase Premium, which compares Bitcoin’s price on Coinbase with global markets, briefly turned positive at the low as U.S. buyers stepped in.
Still, Glassnode stopped short of calling a bottom. Broad demand remains thin: stablecoin supply has shrunk 4.2% over 90 days, and the Coinbase Premium has slipped back to a small discount.
Meanwhile, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs extended their outflow streak to eight sessions on Monday and have bled about $2.2 billion so far in November, according to Decrypt’s ETF tracker.
That makes the $62,000 to $66,000 range the line to watch. Short-term holders bought very few coins below $62,000, and a large cluster of leveraged long positions sits just beneath it, between about $59,500 and $62,200.
A daily close below $62,000 could trigger a fast drop toward the June low of $58,500 and Bitcoin’s realized price of $53,700, the average price at which every coin last moved, Glassnode said.
On the upside, a move back above $74,100, the average cost basis of short-term holders, would confirm that a bottom is forming, according to the firm. Options traders on Deribit, meanwhile, price roughly a one-in-three chance that Bitcoin settles below $53,700 at the September 2027 expiry.
The Fed’s next rate decision is Dec. 9, a day before November inflation data is released.

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 18 日，知名做空机构 Muddy Waters Research 发文宣布做空英伟达，并围绕公司前高管 Ajay K. Puri 与 Super Micro Computer（SMCI）前高管 Cenly Chen 的关系提出质疑。

Muddy Waters 指出，Ajay K. Puri 曾担任英伟达全球销售执行副总裁，是公司最重要的高管之一，于今年 6 月底离职，目前仍担任英伟达高级顾问。该机构注意到，Puri 曾与一名被称为 Cenly Chen 或 Cenly Puri 的女性多次公开同场出现，并质疑其是否就是 SMCI 前首席增长官 Cenly Chen。

今年 3 月，美国检方起诉三名与 SMCI 有关的人员，指控其通过东南亚空壳公司向中国客户非法出售至少 25 亿美元的搭载英伟达 GPU 的服务器。随后，针对 SMCI 的集体诉讼也指称 Cenly Chen 曾负责管理英伟达 GPU 采购及客户分配。

Muddy Waters 强调，目前没有名为 Cenly Chen 的人士遭到政府起诉或刑事指控，相关集体诉讼指控也尚未得到证实。该机构此次提出的是两人身份及关联关系方面的疑问。

items.author: Cointelegraph by Nate Kostar
items.content:
Eastern Europe crypto flows fall 7.9% as Ukraine draws $12B in stablecoins
Chainalysis found that Eastern Europe recorded the steepest decline in crypto activity of any region, while cross-border stablecoin transfers to Ukraine continued amid the ongoing war.
Eastern Europe recorded the steepest decline in cryptocurrency activity among the regions tracked by Chainalysis in the year ended June 2026, falling 7.9% even as retail-sized transfers increased in value, according to a report published Tuesday.
The region’s crypto economy shrank to $642.1 billion from $697.1 billion a year earlier, compared with a 1.6% decline globally, the report states. Russia, which accounted for roughly 44% of the regional total, saw activity fall 14.7% to $284.1 billion over the period. By contrast, Belarus recorded 27.6% growth, while Bulgaria, Moldova and Ukraine saw smaller increases.
The value of transfers of $10,000 or more to crypto services fell 17.4%, from $591.5 billion to $488.6 billion, according to the report.
The value of smaller transfers to crypto services, meanwhile, rose 8.3%. These retail-sized transfers accounted for 13.1% of the value sent to crypto services in Eastern Europe, the highest share of any region studied and above the global average of 10.1%.
Eastern European crypto activity by country, July 2025 to June 2026. Source: Chainalysis report
Polish crypto ATM activity grows
Crypto ATM activity also increased across Eastern Europe, with transaction volumes nearly doubling from $17.3 million to $33.9 million. Poland recorded a 120% increase in ATM transactions despite a 5% decline in centralized exchange activity, with stablecoins accounting for roughly 90% of its ATM transactions.
Chainalysis measures the crypto economy using inflows to crypto services, domestic transfers between personal wallets and cross-border inflows to personal wallets. The figures are measured in dollars, so cryptocurrency price changes can also affect the totals, according to its methodology.
Related: OpenPayd secures MiCA license as stablecoin adoption grows in Europe
Ukraine receives billions in stablecoins
Despite the broader regional decline, Ukraine remained a major destination for stablecoins, receiving $12 billion in cross-border wallet-to-wallet transfers. Of that, $2.41 billion was in retail-sized transfers below $10,000, according to Chainalysis.
Chainalysis also found that countries with larger Ukrainian populations, including prewar diaspora communities and refugees who arrived after Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022, generally sent more stablecoins to Ukraine. Among the 36 countries studied across Europe and North America,
Canada was the largest source of retail-sized, remittance-like transfers, at $359 million.
Crypto transfers to Ukraine by diaspora population, July 2025 to June 2026. Source: Chainalysis report
A Chainalysis spokesperson told Cointelegraph that the cross-border flows were largely denominated in US dollar-pegged stablecoins, although the firm did not provide a breakdown by individual token.
Magazine: Paraguay bank collapse shows stablecoins can offer a lifeline... of sorts
items.title: Eastern Europe crypto flows fall 7.9% as Ukraine draws $12B in stablecoins

items.author: Oluwapelumi Adejumo
items.content:
Quick Take
- A Bitcoin developer verified a 9.39 GB snapshot containing 164.5 million unspent transaction outputs in just 72 seconds.
- The experimental system could significantly reduce Bitcoin node setup times by replacing extensive historical checks with compact cryptographic proofs.
- The developer now wants to integrate the technology into Bitcoin Core, but incomplete validation checks and security requirements remain obstacles.
A Bitcoin developer has shown how to verify a 9.39 GB blockchain snapshot in just 72 seconds, potentially making it easier and faster to run Bitcoin nodes.
The developer, identified as l-henri, disclosed the experiment in a Nov. 13 Delving Bitcoin post, describing a system that uses cryptographic proofs to check Bitcoin's existing transaction records without independently processing its entire history.
The experiment involved a snapshot containing approximately 164.5 million unspent transaction outputs (UTXOs) at Bitcoin block 972,500. These outputs represent Bitcoin that has been received but not yet spent, forming the database nodes use to determine whether coins remain available for transactions.
Using an arm64 computer with approximately 0.5 GB of memory, the developer checked that the snapshot matched the records established by a cryptographic proof.
The process took approximately 72 seconds, with nearly all that time spent reading the 9.39 GB file. Separately, the developer demonstrated that a compact 1.6 MB proof could be verified in a web browser in about half a second.
The achievement could help address a practical challenge of running Bitcoin infrastructure: the time and computing resources required to verify historical blockchain activity before a node becomes fully operational.
How cryptographic proofs could speed up Bitcoin node setup
Bitcoin nodes help secure the network by independently checking transactions and enforcing its rules.
Traditionally, setting up a fully validating node involves downloading and processing BTC's historical transactions to reconstruct the current database of spendable coins.
Bitcoin Core already offers a shortcut through a feature called assumeUTXO, which lets nodes start operating using a snapshot of the blockchain's transaction state. However, the software continues verifying historical transactions in the background to confirm that the snapshot accurately reflects Bitcoin's records.
L-henri's experiment proposes replacing that additional verification work with a cryptographic proof. This approach could let new nodes accept a verified snapshot without repeating extensive historical calculations, potentially reducing setup time and resource requirements.
The developer's system uses STARK proofs, which allow computers to verify specified calculations without repeating every step themselves. In this experiment, the proof covered BTC's block headers from its beginning and checked changes to unspent coins between blocks 935,001 and 972,500.
However, the calculations started from an existing trusted Bitcoin Core snapshot at block 935,000 rather than rebuilding the entire transaction history. The system also excluded checks of transaction scripts and signatures, meaning it does not yet provide the same verification guarantees as a fully validating BTC node.
These limitations remain important as the developer considers integrating the technology into Bitcoin Core.
In the November disclosure, l-henri proposed testing a modification that would let Bitcoin Core accept proof-backed snapshots and skip its existing background validation process.
That would mark a departure from Bitcoin Core's current approach, which independently checks historical records even after loading a snapshot.
The project remains experimental and has not undergone an external security review. Bitcoin Core also does not currently support the proposed integration.
The next step is to test whether the proof system can provide sufficient verification guarantees to replace historical checks without weakening the security assumptions BTC nodes rely on.
items.title: Bitcoin developer verifies 164 million unspent coins in just 72 seconds

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- ARK sold 543,092 Nvidia shares, valued at about $84.8 million using Monday's closing price.
- The firm bought approximately $39.9 million in Block, Circle and Coinbase shares as all three fell.
- ARK also purchased SpaceX stock and sold some crypto-linked holdings, making the day's trades more complicated than a sector-wide switch.
Cathie Wood's ARK Invest sold roughly $85 million worth of Nvidia shares Monday while buying close to $40 million in crypto-exposed stocks, rebalancing exposure to technology and fintech stocks during a broad selloff.
The firm's daily trade file for November 16 shows sales of 543,092 Nvidia shares across two actively managed exchange-traded funds. Using Monday's $156.14 closing price, those shares were worth approximately $84.8 million; the disclosures list share counts rather than the exact prices ARK received.
ARK bought 277,523 shares of payments company Block, worth about $23 million at the close. It also added 180,534 shares of stablecoin issuer Circle, valued at $10.4 million, and 53,760 shares of crypto exchange Coinbase, worth around $6.4 million.
The purchases were spread across funds rather than concentrated in one vehicle. ARK's flagship Innovation ETF (ARKK) bought Circle and most of the Block shares, while its Next Generation Internet ETF (ARKW) bought Coinbase and the remaining Block stock.
Buying the dip, not abandoning AI
All three crypto-linked stocks fell Monday. Circle dropped 7.3%, Coinbase declined 6.1% and Block lost 1.9%, while Nvidia slid 4.1% as investors continued selling technology shares.
That makes the whole movement seem like a shift in holdings, not evidence that ARK expects cryptocurrencies to recover before AI stocks. The manager says its funds can rebalance every trading day, and its trade notifications don't disclose why each position was changed or establish that particular sales financed particular purchases.
ARK had bought 90,443 Nvidia shares just one week earlier, on November 9, during another selloff. The latest sale therefore reverses some of that buying without necessarily suggesting the firm has abandoned the chipmaker or its long-standing investment case for artificial intelligence.
ARK also purchased 378,515 shares of SpaceX, worth roughly $52 million, while selling 30,659 shares of crypto exchange Bullish and units of Ethereum and Solana staking funds. So in this case, Wood would be selling crypto to buy one single AI stock.
Those sales included 300,000 shares of the 3iQ Ethereum Staking ETF and 350,000 shares of the 3iQ Solana Staking ETF. The firm's buying of crypto companies coincided with cuts to other crypto-related investments, a distinction that matters when trying to read a trading strategy from one day's activity.
A familiar bet on crypto infrastructure
Wood has repeatedly bought companies that handle crypto trading and payments during market selloffs. In September, ARK bought $37 million in Block stock in one session, and it previously increased its Circle and Coinbase stakes while reducing exposure to other crypto names.
The companies offer different ways to invest in digital assets without holding tokens directly. Block runs Cash App and Bitcoin-related products; Circle issues the USDC dollar-backed stablecoin; and Coinbase, the only American crypto exchange listed on the stock market, earns revenue from cryptocurrency trading and other services.
ARK's strategy has never been a simple choice between crypto and AI. Its flagship fund already counted Circle, Coinbase and SpaceX among major positions in August, alongside businesses tied to artificial intelligence and financial technology, as earlier holdings showed.
Nvidia's leadership changed five days before Monday's trades. Co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO on November 11, with finance chief Colette Kress appointed interim chief executive, according to the company's SEC filing.
The chipmaker is due to report fiscal third-quarter results after the market closes Tuesday, with a conference call at 5 p.m. Eastern. Those results will give investors their first earnings update since the leadership change—one day after ARK sold more than half a million shares.

items.author: Aaron Wise
items.content:
Most major news outlets’ recent scoops about Nvidia’s suspected evasion of US export controls would sound pretty impressive — if a YouTube channel hadn’t publicly documented the evidence 15 months ago.
Gamers Nexus, which was founded in 2008 by Steve Burke and currently boasts more than 2.7 million subscribers, has been covering this particular story since 2025.
On August 17, 2025, Burke’s team published “The Nvidia AI GPU Black Market,” a three-and-a-half-hour documentary.
In the film, Burke and his crew followed GPUs from American resellers through Southeast Asian brokers to Chinese buyers. The filming stretched across Hong Kong, Shenzhen, and Taipei.
Last night, the US Commerce and Justice departments validated parts of Burke’s investigation, jointly announcing that the Commerce Department has been secretly investigating the company controlled by the lover of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang since 2024.
The press release also confirmed that the Justice Department continues to lead a criminal investigation into Megaspeed’s possible evasion of US export controls of AI chips. For context, evasion of US export controls is a criminal, not merely civil, issue.
Alice Huang, one of at least three women with whom Nvidia’s married CEO has had a romantic affair, was a controlling executive of Megaspeed, a Singaporean company that allegedly assisted with routing money from Chinese companies for the benefit of Nvidia’s export-controlled AI chips.
Her company also allegedly assisted Chinese companies with purchasing cloud compute from Nvidia’s export-controlled chips via data centers in Malaysia and Indonesia.
Nvidia, for its part, has denied wrongdoing. It claims to have instructed customers, including Megaspeed, to honor US export restrictions.
A 2025 documentary about Nvidia chip-smuggling
Burke recapped his reporting yesterday, drawing another 1.3 million views within 24 hours. He titled his video, “If only somebody told us about the GPU smuggling.”
Watching the Wall Street Journal and CNN suddenly cover Nvidia’s alleged GPU smuggling, Burke lamented, “I was too early, man. I was too early.”
The uncomfortable part of this month’s news cycle about Jensen’s problematic relationship with Megaspeed is how much of the story has been public for months.
Read more: Jensen Huang’s exit caps a year of wrecked Nvidia predictions
Nvidia’s problems have been public knowledge since 2025
Indeed, the Financial Times reported in July 2025 that more than $1 billion in banned Nvidia silicon had been smuggled to China, and Gamers Nexus expanded on that evidence with follow-up reporting.
In August 2025, the Justice Department charged two California-based Chinese nationals with allegedly shipping AI chips to China the same August Burke’s film dropped.
The Megaspeed name first drew public scrutiny in October 2025, in a New York Times report that also covered the company’s executive, Alice Huang.
Federal prosecutors even dismantled a $160 million H100 and H200 chip-smuggling ring in December 2025. Both of those series are Nvidia AI chips.
By Februrary 2026, Singapore had already charged three men with fraud over alleged false representations to server suppliers.
Short seller Culper Research disclosed a Nvidia short in May 2026, publicly alleging that over 20% of Nvidia’s fiscal 2026 compute revenue remained driven by China, despite the company’s proclamation that its Chinese revenue was dropping to $0 to honor US export restrictions.
Culper Research also claimed Alibaba secretly financed Megaspeed, and flagged Jensen’s unusually close ties to Alice.
In summary, the public trail of evidence about Nvidia and alleged chip-smuggling has existed for well over a year. The Information now estimates that Alice’s Megaspeed network moved about 240,000 chips worth over $7 billion.
The US government promises to bring “the full extent of the law” against Megaspeed. The evidence of that black market for Nvidia’s export-controlled chips, meanwhile, was available for free on YouTube since 2025.

items.author: Decrypt Staff
items.content:
In brief
- Ethereum’s proposed Glamsterdam upgrade could break up to 15,000 smart contracts, EF developer Marius van der Wijden said on a Nov. 16 core developer call.
- AI-assisted audits by ChainSecurity and Dedaub found ~200 affected contract classes, mostly tied to gas-cost increases.
- No decision was made; removing the changes could delay the upgrade—and the post-quantum roadmap—by four to six months.
Ethereum’s upcoming Glamsterdam upgrade threatens to break as many as 15,000 smart contracts, developers warned during a core developer call Monday, forcing a debate over how much disruption the network should tolerate in the name of scaling.
The concern centers on two proposed changes, EIP-8037 and EIP-8038, designed to let Ethereum scale from 60 million gas to as much as 200 million gas per block, a roughly 3.3x jump that developers say would sharply lower costs for most users while keeping state growth in check.
The problem, flagged late in the development process, is that the changes break certain invariants, assumptions that some smart contracts were built to rely on.
ETH price on November 22, 4:59PM UTC
“Multiple contracts were relying on invariants in the protocol that are modified by 8037 and 8038,” said Marius van der Wijden, an Ethereum Foundation developer who worked on the scaling effort.
He acknowledged that the team “wanted to do significant public outreach” but that timelines slipped amid reorganizations and budget cuts at the foundation. He said he shares “a lot of blame” as the last remaining scaling lead still at the EF.
Two security firms, ChainSecurity and Dedaub, presented findings from AI-assisted audits, with the combined search turning up roughly 200 distinct classes of affected contracts, most tied to gas-cost increases rather than the new mechanics themselves.
Van der Wijden put the highest estimate at 10,000 to 15,000 contracts, a “fringe subset” of Ethereum’s roughly 90 million, with impacted value he loosely pegged in the low hundreds of thousands of dollars among contracts not yet committed to upgrading.
App developers pushed back on the framing. Jango, who builds the Juicebox protocol, warned the change undermines “composability,” a core Ethereum value prop, and shakes “developer confidence in building immutable protocols.” A Uniswap developer urged that EIP-8037 “should definitely be reconsidered.”
The Ethereum Foundation already delayed Glamsterdam’s testnet fork over these gas-related security flaws. Developers stressed Monday that no decision has been made, with the question headed to Thursday’s execution-layer call.
But several signaled a strong desire to ship the fork as planned, arguing that removing the changes could delay Glamsterdam, and the broader roadmap toward post-quantum security, by four to six months, time they say Ethereum can’t spare as quantum and AI threats loom.

items.author: Oluwapelumi Adejumo
items.content:
Quick Take
- Core Lightning's first security patch failed to eliminate a vulnerability that could repeatedly crash Bitcoin payment nodes.
- Attackers could exploit duplicate channel identifiers to keep nodes offline, potentially exposing Bitcoin held in unrelated payment channels.
- A second patch closed the remaining attack route in September, but operators running outdated software remain exposed.
Bitcoin's Core Lightning software required two security patches to eliminate a vulnerability that could repeatedly crash payment nodes and potentially expose funds held in other channels.
A Nov. 13 security disclosure revealed that an initial repair released in July failed to address a second attack method that could keep affected nodes offline even after they restarted.
The vulnerability, tracked as LNF-2026-0004, affected Core Lightning, one of the software implementations used to operate nodes on Bitcoin's Lightning Network.
Security researcher Nishant Bansal discovered that attackers could exploit how Core Lightning assigned identifiers to payment channels, creating duplicate records that caused the software to crash.
The weakness originated in the network's channel-opening process, where each payment channel receives an identifier derived from the Bitcoin transaction output that funds it. Core Lightning could accept multiple channels referencing the same funding output, producing identical identifiers that conflicted with assumptions in its internal software.
In the first attack, a malicious peer could create duplicate pending channels and crash a victim's node simply by reconnecting. The attack required no Bitcoin transaction fees because the fraudulent channels did not need on-chain funding. Each subsequent reconnection could trigger another crash, allowing attackers to repeatedly interrupt payment processing.
However, researchers identified a more persistent variation involving previously closed channels.
By reusing an identifier associated with a closed channel and subsequently closing another channel with the same identifier, attackers could trigger a software failure that persisted across restarts.
Unlike the initial attack, this method required on-chain transaction fees but could leave the node unable to recover without a software upgrade.
Why Core Lightning's first security patch failed
Core Lightning developers addressed the original vulnerability in version 26.06.6, released on July 22, after researchers privately reported the reconnection attack earlier that month.
The update prevented new channels from reusing funding outputs associated with existing live channels. It also modified connection handling to prevent duplicate records already stored from triggering the original crash.
However, the protection did not extend to identifiers associated with closed channels, leaving the second attack route available.
Researcher Crypt-iQ independently identified the remaining weakness, prompting developers to introduce broader safeguards in version 26.06.8, released Sept. 22.
The second update expanded duplicate-identifier checks across active and closed channels belonging to different peers. It also allowed nodes containing previously stored duplicate records to recover without repeatedly crashing.
The potential financial consequences extended beyond disrupted Lightning payments.
According to the advisory, nodes forced offline could lose the ability to monitor Bitcoin's blockchain for attempts to settle channels using revoked transaction states.
That could allow dishonest counterparties to claim funds using outdated channel balances. Offline nodes could also miss deadlines for collecting time-sensitive payments, placing Bitcoin held in unrelated channels at risk.
The researchers did not report confirmed exploitation or financial losses.
The findings affect Core Lightning versions preceding the complete September repair, with the reconnection vulnerability dating back to version 0.12.0 and the persistent closed-channel crash introduced in version 25.05.
Developers have since released additional security updates, including version 26.06.10, which addresses other vulnerabilities involving channel operations, payment resolution, and remote crashes.
Core Lightning's maintainers have urged operators to upgrade to the latest release to protect their nodes against the disclosed weaknesses.
items.title: Bitcoin Lightning developers needed two patches to stop a potentially costly attack

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- Jensen Huang said he would return as Nvidia CEO if the board decided it was in the company's best interests.
- His X profile dropped the CEO title as an independent investigation into his conduct continues.
- Reports say directors are not considering his return, despite support from Trump and Musk and expressions of sympathy from Sam Altman.
Jensen Huang said Tuesday he would be willing to return as Nvidia CEO, publicly addressing the campaign to reinstate him less than a week after his abrupt departure. His offer came despite reports that the chipmaker's board has no plans to bring him back.
“If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO,” Huang wrote in a statement on X.
The Nvidia co-founder also apologized for the conduct that triggered his exit. “I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life,” he wrote. “I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret.”
“I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation,” he added.
Over the past week, I’ve been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I've never met. Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me.
I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an…
— Jensen Huang (@JensenHuang) November 17, 2026
His X profile underwent a separate change around the same time. By Tuesday, Huang had removed “CEO” from his bio, which now identifies him only as “Founder of NVIDIA”; the company banner and corporate affiliation badge also disappeared.
Huang resigned last Thursday after 33 years leading the chipmaker he founded in 1993. His departure followed disclosures about extramarital relationships involving Nvidia employees and a business executive whom U.S. officials suspect of connections to Chinese intelligence. Those intelligence allegations have not been established as fact.
The board's independent investigation is examining his conduct and whether sensitive company information or national security were put at risk. Nvidia has said it has no reason to believe company secrets were compromised; chief financial officer Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO.
A comeback campaign meets a reluctant board
“Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” Huang wrote. He said many were reaching out directly as Nvidia navigates “complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics.” “NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company,” he added.
But the board's position—at least as of Tuesday—is that directors are focused on the investigation, not reinstatement.
The company is simultaneously looking for a successor. Directors reportedly approached Arm CEO Rene Haas, a former Nvidia executive, according to the Financial Times, although Nvidia said it had not formally engaged candidates and called speculation premature.
The movement to restore Huang has nevertheless attracted powerful allies. President Donald Trump said Monday he “would certainly not mind” a comeback, while Elon Musk backed a petition demanding Huang's reinstatement that had drawn nearly 192,000 signatures by Monday.
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman offered a more qualified defense. Altman, who was briefly fired and reinstated at OpenAI in 2023, said Huang had “long been a hero of mine” and that “heroes have flaws,” but stopped short of saying Nvidia should rehire him.
Huang also made a patriotic appeal, especially considering his outsting was especially rushed not because of his affairs but because of the possibility of him leaking secrets to China. “I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life,” he wrote.
“NVIDIA has been my life’s work,” he continued. “Nowhere but in America could a company like NVIDIA be possible. I love our country, and I love NVIDIA.”
He closed by thanking supporters and telling his family, “I love you, and I will spend the rest of my life being worthy of yours.” Nvidia, meanwhile, is continuing its permanent CEO search, with Kress scheduled to lead the company's quarterly earnings call later today.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Adrian Zmudzinski
items.content:
Lighter incident exposes risks beyond withdrawal controls
Crypto platforms need enforceable limits on every route an API key can use to transfer value, including trades, internal transfers and shared pools.
A recent incident where over $10 million was siphoned out of a decentralized perpetual futures exchange shows the shortcomings of focusing security on withdrawal controls
According to Lighter’s postmortem, an attacker used compromised API keys to move funds into a public pool and redeem shares held through another account. Bitquery traced a withdrawal of 10.39 million USDC. The exchange said its protocol and smart contracts were unaffected.
Lighter now requires wallet signatures for transfers into public pools and has made API-key signatures non-public. It also plans IP allowlists and configurable permissions for individual keys.
Lighter has since restored deposits and withdrawals while also returning about $5 million in USDC (USDC) to the affected trader.
Lighter incident infographic. Source: Bitquery
The incident highlights how cybersecurity reviews need to look past smart contract vulnerabilities. It is important to also consider the gap between the permissions a system grants and the financial consequences those permissions allow.
Related: Google says hackers use AI agents to find and exploit software flaws
The real risk involving a credential depends on the balances it can reach, the transactions it can initiate and the exposures it can create. Whether it is permitted to withdraw assets and to which destinations are just two of many factors. As Lighter put it in its postmortem:
“A key that can trade can still lose you money if someone else holds it.”
This means that a user needs to establish a clear mandate for each credential. The mandate can specify accessible accounts, permitted markets, order sizes, pricing tolerances and aggregate exposure. Moving capital into a shared pool or expanding those limits can require separate authorization.
The same logic applies to additional signatures. A second signature adds meaningful protection when its approval process independently evaluates the transaction’s financial effect.
To read the full analysis on how DEX permissions go beyond withdrawals, sign up for the Daybreak Newsletter.

items.author: Mark Toon
items.content:
Anton and James Peraire-Bueno, brothers who ran an Ethereum validator to exploit MEV bots for $25 million in April 2023, have been acquitted of wire fraud and money laundering charges.
A weeks-long trial last November resulted in a deadlocked jury and was ultimately deemed a mistrial.
Judge Jessica Clarke ruled on Monday that “the government failed to prove that the Peraire-Buenos made any material misrepresentations in the execution of their scheme.”
Judge Clarke’s opinion is limited to whether the evidence presented at trial was sufficient to achieve a conviction on the charges presented. It doesn’t, however, comment on whether the brothers’ behaviour was “right or moral, or even whether it violated uncharged crimes.”
Read more: MEV bot JaredFromSubway.eth loses $7.5M to approvals honeypot
Code is Law
The Peraire-Bueno brothers made around $25 million in just 12 seconds off a bait-and-switch exploit of MEV trading bots in April 2023. Soon after exploiting this design flaw in Flashbots’ MEV-boost relay, the pair disclosed a different exploit under the moniker “Low Carb Crusader.”
Nonetheless, they were indicted in May 2024 on federal charges which prosecutors at the time dubbed a “first-of-its kind wire fraud and money laundering scheme.”
The full list of charges was wire fraud, conspiracy to commit wire fraud, conspiracy to commit money laundering, and conspiracy to receive stolen property.
Judge Clarke ruled, however, that none of the brothers’ actions construed a “material misrepresentation” to the victims, an aspect key to a wire fraud conviction.
Moreover, she concluded that Ethereum is a “trustless, highly adversarial environment with no terms of use… without the safeguards that exist in regulated markets.”
Clarke recognised that the brothers’ scheme “may have frustrated the spirit of MEV-Boost’s ‘design,’ [it] made no misrepresentation in its execution that can form the basis for fraud.”
She compares the case to that of Avraham Eisenberg’s 2022 exploit of Mango Markets, charges relating to which were ultimately overturned via similar reasoning last year.
Read more: Avi Eisenberg seeks leniency in child porn and crypto sentencing
Crypto lawyers have praised the decision in invalidating the prosecution’s “honest validator” theory which Coin Center’s Peter Van Valkenburgh worried would let the government “impose its own code of conduct on Ethereum validators.”
The younger brother, Anton Peraire-Bueno, who goes by “Curious Rabbit” on X thanked family and friends who had “rearranged their lives around this case” since the indictment, adding, “in the end, it’s a good story when the good guys win.”
James echoed his brother’s sentiments, and is apparently looking forward to a celebratory beer.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Nate Kostar
items.content:
Fed’s Waller cites Binance hack in warning over tokenized finance
Fed Governor Christopher Waller questioned who bears responsibility for fraud, compromised keys and failed transactions as traditional financial assets move onto blockchains.
US Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller cited the recent $6.3 billion Binance hack while raising questions about security and accountability in tokenized financial markets, suggesting that major institutional transactions may require blockchain systems offering greater privacy and control.
Speaking at The Clearing House’s annual conference in New York on Nov. 17, an event bringing together banking and payments industry leaders, Waller questioned who would bear responsibility when fraudsters exploit smart contracts, private keys are compromised, transfers go wrong or assets become stranded on failed blockchains.
Waller said the level of security and oversight required could depend on the importance of the financial transactions involved:
For example, systemically important financial transactions may call for the most conservative designs. These designs might trade some of the developer creativity found on purely permissionless, open networks in favor of greater privacy and control.
The expansion of tokenized finance would also require clear legal frameworks governing ownership rights, custody and settlement, he said, arguing that governance and legal protections are as important as technical safeguards in building trust.
Waller’s remarks came as four Democratic senators pressed the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) over safeguards for tokenized stocks. In a letter released Monday, the lawmakers questioned who would be responsible for shares transferred outside regulated platforms and whether regulators could freeze or recover the tokens.
Related: Custodia Bank loses Supreme Court bid for direct Fed payment access
Barr warns of AI-related cybersecurity risks
Waller wasn’t the only Federal Reserve governor to raise concerns about emerging financial technologies this week. His remarks followed a Monday speech by fellow Fed Governor Michael Barr, who warned that artificial intelligence could introduce new cybersecurity risks as financial institutions increasingly adopt the technology.
Barr said AI-enabled attackers were exploiting vulnerabilities previously considered too difficult to target, while autonomous AI systems could behave in ways that undermine security controls
“Attackers only need to be right once, while defenders need to be right all the time,” Barr said.
He also said major banks had reported finding AI agents attempting to take actions in retail customer accounts without being able to verify their authenticity or authorization, highlighting the need for stronger authentication and security controls.

items.author: Oluwapelumi Adejumo
items.content:
Quick Take
- Google uncovered an AI hacking framework capable of turning software security patches into exploits and launching attacks automatically.
- The system could help hackers target vulnerable websites before security updates are installed, sharply reducing the time available for protection.
- Google warns that increasingly autonomous hacking tools could accelerate cyberattacks as criminals automate vulnerability discovery and exploitati
Google has uncovered an AI-powered hacking system capable of transforming software security fixes into automated attacks against vulnerable websites.
In a Nov. 16 report, Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant revealed that attackers were using AI frameworks to identify vulnerabilities, generate malicious code, and execute exploits with minimal human involvement.
The researchers discovered one such system, dubbed exploit_agent, on an exposed staging server containing multiple AI models connected to cybersecurity research and exploitation tools.
The framework was configured to monitor software updates, compare patched code with older versions, and identify weaknesses that developers had recently repaired. It could subsequently generate attack code and execute it automatically, allowing attackers to target websites that had not yet installed the relevant security updates.
This approach exploits the information developers publish when addressing software vulnerabilities. Changes made to repair a flaw can inadvertently reveal how the underlying weakness could be exploited.
Google said the technique lets attackers focus on known vulnerabilities rather than spend time discovering previously unknown security flaws.
The company's investigation also uncovered stolen victim data and malicious scripts capable of conducting internal network reconnaissance, brute-force attacks and installing webshells that provide remote access to compromised servers.
Some tools could remove webshells left by competing attackers, potentially helping the operator retain control over compromised systems.
Google found evidence that the operator was particularly interested in French websites associated with media, entertainment, and education. One recovered example showed the framework examining access-control protections in Spectra, a WordPress plugin used for website development.
The discovery marked the first time Google had identified attackers using AI frameworks to fully automate vulnerability discovery and exploitation without human intervention throughout the process.
North Korean hackers turn AI development tools against crypto companies
Google's report also revealed a separate campaign in which suspected North Korean hackers exploited AI-powered development tools to infiltrate cryptocurrency organizations in North America and Europe.
The attackers, tracked as MIDNIGHT NEPTUNE, combined AI-generated identities with fraudulent recruitment campaigns to gain access to corporate systems.
They created fake recruiter profiles on professional networking platforms using AI-generated photographs, then directed prospective victims to fraudulent meeting websites.
Those websites instructed victims to run supposed troubleshooting commands that instead executed malicious scripts.
Once inside an organization, the attackers accessed internal code repositories and modified configuration files used by Anthropic's Claude Code development assistant.
The altered files were designed to automatically download a backdoor known as SOMBERMEME whenever employees launched Claude Code.
Google also discovered that the attackers disguised GitHub access tokens using names associated with Microsoft Copilot, concealing their movements within compromised development environments.
The campaign expanded on North Korea's established use of AI to generate fake resumes, prepare for job interviews, and impersonate Western technology workers seeking remote employment.
Google said the latest intrusions showed how attackers exploited AI development tools already embedded in corporate workflows to distribute malicious software.
Meanwhile, the emergence of autonomous exploitation frameworks threatens to accelerate attacks against organizations running outdated software.
Google warned that automating vulnerability analysis and exploit execution could substantially reduce the time between disclosing a security flaw and exploiting it, leaving website operators with increasingly narrow windows to install protective updates.
items.title: Google uncovers AI hacking tool that turns security fixes into cyberattacks

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- A wallet tied to the October 29 Binance hack sent 34,279.66 ETH, worth roughly $63 million, to three new addresses on Tuesday after remaining inactive since October 30.
- On-chain data shows 74,880 ETH, worth about $136.8 million, moving from hack-linked wallets and some funds were being swapped for Bitcoin through Thorchain.
- The Justice Department has court authority to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion tied to the theft, but transfers between wallets do not establish that stolen crypto has been cashed out.
Wallets linked to the $6.3 billion Binance hack started moving large amounts of stolen Ethereum on Tuesday, breaking more than two weeks of inactivity as U.S. authorities continue trying to recover the funds.
Blockchain security service MistTrack reported that one address associated with the October 29 theft sent 34,279.66 ETH, worth roughly $63 million at the time, to three newly created wallets. The address had not moved its funds since October 30.
The on-chain record shows three outgoing transactions shortly before 7 a.m. UTC: two transfers of 12,000 ETH ($21.2 million) each and a third of about 10,279.66 ETH ($18.2 million). MistTrack said the receiving wallets had not sent the ether onward when it posted its initial alert.
That $63 million movement was only part of Tuesday’s activity. A second wallet linked to the same hack transferred another 40,600.66 ETH, worth roughly $74 million, across five transactions.
Analytics firm Arkham shows wallets linked to the attack had transferred a combined 74,880 ETH, valued at $136.8 million, over roughly three hours, and funds were beginning to be swapped for Bitcoin through Thorchain, a service that moves and exchanges crypto between blockchains.
Stolen crypto, frozen assets
The transfers come five days after the Justice Department said courts had authorized it to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion connected to the Binance theft. That sum is part of more than $2.7 billion frozen through combined government and private-sector action, not an additional recovery on top of it.
The FBI has attributed the attack to TraderTraitor, a hacking operation it links to North Korea’s military. The October 29 breach drained roughly $6.43 billion from Binance across 11 blockchains, according to blockchain analytics company Elliptic, making it the largest known crypto theft. North Korea denied involvement.
ETH price on November 22, 4:59PM UTC
The attackers rushed to convert stablecoins into assets their issuers could not freeze. Tether and Circle can block stolen tokens on their networks, but ordinary ETH and Bitcoin do not have a central company capable of stopping a particular wallet from sending them.
Elliptic’s November 16 analysis put the frozen or seized portion at $2.85 billion and said the main Bitcoin and ETH holdings were still sitting in attack-linked addresses. That was before Tuesday’s transfers, which show at least part of the previously stationary ETH has begun moving.
Moving money is not cashing out
Investigators have already traced stolen Binance assets through decentralized exchanges, cross-chain transfers and privacy services. Elliptic found about $267 million had been converted into Bitcoin by November 16, while about $2.55 billion remained in addresses associated with the theft at that day’s prices.
The attackers had also spread their activity across almost 27,000 wallets and more than 83,000 transactions. That complicated trail does not mean they have managed to turn most of the stolen assets into cash.
Elliptic said only a negligible amount had likely been cashed out as of its latest assessment. To do that at scale, the holders would typically need an exchange or an over-the-counter broker willing to take the funds, creating another point at which authorities could identify and potentially block them.

items.author: Simon Willison
items.content:
Datasette Lite is my port of the Datasette Python application to run directly in the browser using WebAssembly and Pyodide. I've released a complete rewrite of Datasette Lite using service workers, and it's now almost indistinguishable from the real server-side application.

You can now do all of the following, using a carefully crafted URL to lite.datasette.io:

  • Load client-side Datasette to browse any SQLite database, JSON file, CSV file or SQL script
  • Select a released version of Datasette to load from PyPI
  • Load a specific commit, tag, or branch name from the Datasette GitHub repository
  • Pick from over 100 versions of SQLite to use with Datasette
  • Install additional Datasette plugins from PyPI or URLs to wheel files, including JavaScript visualization tools

The ability to load specific Datasette references, plugins, and SQLite versions makes this a fantastic tool for linking to demos of work-in-progress features or bug reproductions, without needing to spin up a full web server to serve that demo.

As an example, consider the following URL:

https://lite.datasette.io/?install=datasette-maplibre&url=https://gist.githubusercontent.com/simonw/39fa5d399465766039549912e2b3d291/raw/f6dfba99a75cbb8b5d9386223220eb52272767ee/demo.db&metadata=https://gist.githubusercontent.com/simonw/39fa5d399465766039549912e2b3d291/raw/f6dfba99a75cbb8b5d9386223220eb52272767ee/metadata.yml#/demo/capitals_and_countries%23map=0/4.2/180&color=continent

Follow that link and, after a short loading screen, you'll find yourself on a page that looks like this:

That's Datasette running the new datasette-maplibre plugin, loading up a database of GeoJSON shapes of countries and displaying both a combined map and individual boundary maps in a table.

Let's break down that URL to see what it's doing:

https://lite.datasette.io/
  ?install=datasette-maplibre
  &url=https://.../demo.db
  &metadata=https://.../metadata.yml
  #/demo/capitals_and_countries%23map=0/4.2/180&color=continent

The ?install=datasette-maplibre installs that additional plugin from PyPI. You can pass &install=... as many times as you like to load more plugins.

&url=https://.../demo.db loads that SQLite database from the provided URL. These URLs need to have open CORS headers - I host files like this in Gists, because they provide an easy way to get open CORS headers on a web-hosted file.

&metadata=https://.../metadata.yml loads this metadata.yml file. The metadata file adds HTML descriptions to various tables, and to the Datasette homepage. Visit that homepage here for a guided tour of the other features of that plugin, all defined in the metadata file.

#/demo/capitals_and_countries%23map=0/4.2/180&color=continent is a fragment hash that turns into a location within Datasette - here it's loading the /demo/capitals_and_countries SQL view, then appending another fragment hash to it (%23 is a URL-encoded #) which tells the map plugin to zoom to a certain location and to set the color of the shapes on the map based on the continent column in the data.

That URL is doing a lot of work! I wrote more about this trick for building URL-addressable software in URL-addressable Pyodide Python environments last year.

The full set of supported URL arguments is described in the Datasette Lite README.

I've already started using Datasette Lite as part of the Datasette development process. Here's a recent issue describing a pagination bug - I posted a comment there demonstrating the old, broken behavior and the new fix using links to Datasette Lite:

Demo of the bug: https://lite.datasette.io/?ref=1.0a42&sql=https://gist.github.com/simonw/75ececf61d50e6e8d50f0c150150ee81#/data/scores?_size=2&_sort=score - click next and the second page is empty.

Here's that same page with the bug fixed (running on 1.0a43): https://lite.datasette.io/?ref=1.0a43&sql=https://gist.github.com/simonw/75ececf61d50e6e8d50f0c150150ee81#/data/scores?_size=2&_sort=score

How this works, using service workers

Datasette Lite is not a new project. I launched the first version back in 2022, originally as a bit of a joke (running server-side apps in the browser is pretty funny) but one that quickly started proving its value.

The problem with that initial version is that it was a hack. It worked by running Datasette in a Pyodide web worker, simulating requests through that stack, then injecting the resulting HTML back into the top level page using innerHTML.

This worked for basic Datasette, but meant that any feature that used JavaScript failed to work, because script tags in innerHTML don't execute, and the web worker tricks it used failed to load additional JavaScript or CSS files.

The new version takes a completely different approach based on Service Workers. These allow JavaScript to intercept HTTP requests for new pages and resources and serve them from client-side code instead.

Datasette Lite registers a service worker for the entire lite.datasette.io domain. The parent page then creates an iframe that sends requests for Datasette pages to URLs that look like this:

/app/aa94e6851595/ # the homepage (HTML)
/app/aa94e6851595/data/places # a table page (HTML)
/app/aa94e6851595/-/static/navigation-search.js # (JavaScript)
/app/aa94e6851595/-/static/app.css # (CSS)

Those are regular Datasette URLs, but with a /app/aa94e6851595/ prefix. What's that about?

The /app/<session>/ prefix is necessary because of multiple tabs.

Consider the URL above, which loads the demo instance with the datasette-maplibre plugin. That URL defines a full, custom Datasette instance. You might have that one running in a tab, then one of my other demo links running in another.

The service worker for lite.datasette.io is shared between all of those tabs. If it routed to a single instance of Datasette then every tab would share that underlying instance, no matter what plugins or other settings their URL attempted to configure.

Instead, the parent page generates a random session ID and uses it as a prefix for all of the subsequent hidden asset and page loads. The service worker can then use that session ID to route those requests back through the parent page to a web worker running a dedicated Datasette instance for that particular session.

(We still need a web worker because Pyodide in a service worker would not be able to maintain state beyond around 30 seconds, depending on the browser. There are a lot of moving parts here!)

I had Claude Fable 5.2 generate several SVG diagrams to help explain this. Here's my favorite of those, now embedded in the Datasette Lite README:

This system started life back in May as an AI research spike generated using Claude Opus 4.8. It wasn't until November (and Claude Fable 5.2) that I felt familiar enough with how it all works to confidently ship it to production!

Bonus feature: pick your version of SQLite

I added this feature last night as an off-shoot of investigating a potential bug in SQLite.

Datasette is meant to work against any released version of SQLite since 3.25 (released in September 2018). There have been 87 further releases since then.

Being able to fire up Datasette against a specific version of SQLite is really useful for demonstrating new SQLite features and debugging weird issues.

In the past I've used various tricks to get different SQLite versions running with Python on my Mac, but it's not a trivial process.

WebAssembly is perfect for this. I can load up a custom SQLite build entirely in my browser, test it there, then discard it when I close my tab.

datasette/pysqlite3-wasm-wheels is my new repository which contains WebAssembly compiled Python wheels for pysqlite3 for 163 different SQLite versions. Each version gets a file with a name like this:

pysqlite3-0.6.2-3.54.1-cp314-cp314-pyemscripten_2026_0_wasm32.whl

That's for SQLite 3.54.1, the most recent version.

Datasette Lite now takes a special ?sqlite= URL parameter, which will accept a version number like 3.54.1, resolve the path to the corresponding wheel file, then fetch that wheel and install it into the Pyodide environment and configure Datasette to use it.

Once I'd built the wheels, I decided to have Claude Fable 5.2 build me [this bonus tool](https://datasette.github.io/pysqlite3-wasm-wheels/?versions=3.54.1,3.54.0&sql=select+json_object(%27a%27%2C+(select+json_array(1%29%29%29) for comparing a SQL query across any selected versions of SQLite. Here's an example showing how select json_object('a', (select json_array(1))) differs between SQLite 3.54.0 and 3.54.1:

This should work for every other Python app, too

Nothing about how Datasette Lite works is unique to Datasette. Almost any Python application should be able to pull the same trick - running entirely in the browser using WebAssembly and Pyodide, as a cheap way to provide preview environments, demonstrate features, and recreate bugs.

C and Rust extensions used to be a blocker for this kind of thing, but any good coding agent can compile those to Pyodide-compatible WebAssembly now. You can even publish them to PyPI as of PEP 783 in April 2026.

One catch is databases. SQLite is no problem at all, but running PostgreSQL or MySQL in WebAssembly, while possible, is still a path less trodden.

I'd love to see WebAssembly preview environments like these become a common pattern across the Python ecosystem.

For Hacker News: Full server-side Datasette Python app in the browser with service workers

You are only seeing the long-form articles from my blog. Subscribe to /atom/everything/ to get all of my posts, or take a look at my other subscription options.
items.title: Running the full server-side Datasette Python app in the browser with service workers and Pyodide

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 18 日，glassnode 发文表示，比特币近期暴跌引发大规模投降式抛售，已实现亏损升至历史局部底部附近的水平，杠杆多头也遭到集中清算。11 月 13 日至 14 日，多头清算规模相对于未平仓合约总量达到 2023 年以来较高水平。当前，比特币在 6.2 万至 6.6 万美元区间获得支撑，该区域聚集了约五分之一的短期持有者筹码，并在两天集中抛售期间增加约 6.6 万枚 BTC。

不过，比特币整体市场需求仍然疲软。过去 90 天，稳定币总供应量下降 4.2%；美国现货比特币 ETF 在截至 11 月 13 日的 10 个交易日内净流出 26 亿美元。此外，MARA 和 Riot 本月已出售约 2.8 万枚 BTC，以支持向 AI 及高性能计算数据中心业务转型，而 Strategy 仍在持续增持。若比特币日线收盘跌破 6.2 万美元，短期持有者可能进一步承压，叠加下方杠杆多头清算集中的风险，价格或快速下探至 5.85 万美元的 6 月低点，甚至 5.37 万美元的已实现价格。反之，若重新站上 7.41 万美元的短期持有者成本基础，则将进一步确认市场底部形成的可能性。

此外，尽管比特币市场资金需求低迷，加密行业的现实世界资产（RWA）代币化进程仍在持续推进。今年以来，链上活跃代币化产品数量已从年初的 428 种增长至 11 月初的约 6200 种；交易平台 RWA 永续合约数量也从约 190 种增至 3200 种以上，相关合约未平仓合约规模从 3.5 亿美元扩大至约 150 亿美元。

items.content:
In brief
- Former Robinhood engineer Huaisong Xiang pleaded guilty to wire fraud over trades ahead of cryptocurrency listing announcements.
- He agreed to forfeit $125,523 in profits from Hyperliquid perpetual futures, according to federal prosecutors.
- Xiang faces up to 20 years in prison, with sentencing scheduled for February 25, 2027.
Former Robinhood software engineer Huaisong “Jerry” Xiang pleaded guilty Monday to wire fraud for using confidential plans for upcoming cryptocurrency listings to trade on Hyperliquid. The 30-year-old agreed to forfeit $125,523 in profits from the scheme, according to the Justice Department.
Xiang entered his plea before U.S. District Judge Colleen McMahon on November 16, two months after prosecutors accused him and another Robinhood engineer of trading ahead of the brokerage's token announcements. He pleaded guilty to one count of wire fraud; the DOJ announcement did not report a guilty plea to the commodities-fraud charge initially brought against him.
As a software engineer working on new listings for Robinhood Crypto, Xiang had access to a private Slack channel reserved for employees classified as “Coin Aware Individuals.” It contained information about which tokens were coming to the platform and when, according to the FBI complaint filed in September.
ETH price on November 22, 4:59PM UTC
Robinhood's internal policy prohibited that group from trading around upcoming listings on any platform, not just Robinhood. The restriction began before a listing was announced and continued for 24 hours after it became public. A November 2024 email warned Xiang to “refrain from abusing access to or knowledge of this information,” the complaint says.
Investigators described one trade involving POPCAT, a Solana-based meme coin. After receiving internal messages about a planned March 13, 2025 listing, Xiang moved approximately 18 Ethereum, then worth about $34,000, into a Hyperliquid wallet and opened a bullish position tied to POPCAT, according to the complaint.
He closed that position at a profit after the token became available on Robinhood but before the company published its listing announcement, the FBI alleged. The complaint identified at least 10 other occasions through February 2026 when the same wallet traded ahead of announcements, including positions involving MEW, MOODENG, ONDO and RENDER.
Hyperliquid's perpetual futures let traders speculate on a cryptocurrency's price without owning the token itself. Unlike conventional futures, the contracts have no expiration date, and a “long” position gains value if the underlying token's price rises.
New listings can increase a token's exposure to buyers and put upward pressure on its price. Prosecutors said Xiang used his advance knowledge to position himself for those moves, sometimes closing his trades before the public knew Robinhood had added the asset.
“No matter the trading platform, corporate insiders will be held accountable when they trade based on misappropriated information,” U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald said in Monday's announcement.
Robinhood said in September that it had investigated the matter, reported it to authorities and maintained a zero-tolerance policy on insider trading.
Xiang faces a statutory maximum of 20 years in prison, although the judge will decide his sentence. He is scheduled to appear before McMahon for sentencing on February 25, 2027.

「大空头」Michael Burry继续加仓Adobe，认为华尔街低估其长期价值

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 18 日，「大空头」原型人物 Michael Burry 通过其 Substack 账号发文表示，继续增持 Adobe（ADBE）。此前，他曾在股价约 246 美元时进一步买入。Burry 认为，市场目前将 Adobe 视为一家失去增长前景的公司，但实际上其估值仍具吸引力，甚至是其投资范围内估值最低的软件公司。

items.author: Cointelegraph by William Suberg
items.content:
Bitcoin drops 2.5% as Nvidia stock risks new 5-month lows into Q3 earnings
Bitcoin price downside sees local lows of $63,269 as Nvidia stock targets $150 as traders brace for volatility over Q3 earnings.
Bitcoin saw selling pressure after Tuesday’s Wall Street open as stock markets stayed on edge ahead of Nvidia’s third-quarter earnings and forward guidance.
Key points:
- Bitcoin (BTC) threatens its intraday range between $64,000 and $66,000 as risk assets wait for key earnings guidance from Nvidia.
- The company’s former CEO Jensen Huang is due to testify before US Congress on Dec. 1 as analysis gives less than 20% odds of his reinstatement.
- BTC price analysis says reclaiming a key bull-market support trend line at $67,977 is insufficient to confirm a market rebound.
Bitcoin, stocks face Nvidia headwinds ahead of earnings
Data from TradingView showed BTC/USD dipping to $63,269 on Bitstamp, down up to 2.5% on the day.
BTC/USD one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
US equities saw minor losses as the session began, with traders eyeing key data from Nvidia, along with cues as to how the company planned to handle the ongoing controversy surrounding its former CEO Jensen Huang.
Amid mounting pressure to reinstate Huang despite resistance from US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, commentators saw little chance of Nvidia’s board reversing its decision to dismiss him.
On Tuesday, the board announced the creation of a National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee, dedicated to “oversight of the company’s national security policies, export control compliance and global trade risk management.”
“We are committed to working constructively with government and industry partners to help establish and advance a robust framework that uses every tool at our disposal to safeguard national security while supporting continued technological innovation,” board chairman Harvey Jones commented in a press release.
Huang will also appear to testify before Congress on Dec. 1. In its latest analysis, trading resource The Kobeissi Letter put the odds of Huang returning at less than 20% in light of the latest events.
“Any indication that the probability is higher would be strongly bullish for the stock,” it wrote on X.
Kobeissi queried whether Huang’s departure could justify the $750 billion loss in market cap Nvidia had suffered, with NVDA dipping to $150.35, down over 3% on the day. On Nov. 12, it hit $148.80, its lowest since late June.
Nvidia stock one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Market nerves extended beyond the US ahead of a key moment for the AI sector. South Korea’s tech-heavy KOSPI Composite Index finished Tuesday’s trading session 2.6% lower at 4,968 points — its lowest daily close since Feb. 2.
KOSPI one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
“The tape feels increasingly fragile as Nvidia’s AI premium continues to unwind and investors reassess the durability of the ecosystem built around its dominance,” CNBC quoted FedWatch Advisors founder Ben Emons as stating in a note.
CNBC and others referenced data from Bank of America’s latest monthly fund manager survey, which showed that investors slashed tech-stock exposure last month from 37% to 12% overweight tech — the largest single monthly reduction since June 2006.
Analyst: BTC price must avoid rebound “trap”
BTC price action sought to break down from its narrow range between $64,000 and $66,000, in place since Nov. 15, as traders awaited Nvidia signals.
Related: Bitcoin realized loss metric beats June high as open interest eyes 2-year low
In an X update on the day, Keith Alan, cofounder of crypto trading platform Material Indicators, stipulated that the market needed to fulfil several key conditions as part of a durable rebound.
BTC/USD, he argued, should reclaim its 200-week simple moving average (SMA) at $67,977, but that this alone was not “enough.” Lower time frames must also produce a series of higher swing lows and higher swing highs, with breakouts through local resistance accompanied by high buyer volume.
“Until then, a bounce has a higher probability of being a trap than a legit recovery effort,” Alan summarized.
Previously, Cointelegraph reported on the status of the 200-week SMA as a key level to defend as support as part of a bear-market recovery.
BTC/USD one-day chart with the 200-week SMA. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
items.title: Bitcoin drops 2.5% as Nvidia stock risks new 5-month lows into Q3 earnings

items.author: Oluwapelumi Adejumo
items.content:
Quick Take
- BlackRock's Bitcoin ETF ended an 11-session, $2.35 billion withdrawal streak after attracting $76.5 million on Monday.
- IBIT remains $2.1 billion positive for 2026, while the broader Bitcoin ETF market has suffered $1.8 billion in net withdrawals.
- Wintermute warns Bitcoin remains in a bear market, with a recovery above $68,000 and renewed ETF demand needed to ease selling pressure.
BlackRock's Bitcoin ETF ended an 11-session outflow streak totaling $2.35 billion on Monday, even as the broader market remained underwater for 2026.
The iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) attracted $76.5 million on Nov. 16, recording its first positive session since Oct. 29, according to Farside Investors.
The inflow helped US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds post a combined $7.9 million gain, ending seven consecutive trading sessions of withdrawals totaling approximately $1.91 billion.
However, BlackRock accounted for the entire recovery. Seven competing funds collectively lost $68.6 million, while four recorded no net flows.
Grayscale's GBTC led Monday's withdrawals with $34.6 million, followed by Fidelity's FBTC at $11.3 million. ARKB, BTCO, EZBC, MSBT and Grayscale's smaller BTC trust also registered outflows.
US spot Bitcoin ETFs reported combined net inflows of $7.9 million. Positive values indicate net inflows and negative values indicate net outflows. Four funds reported $0.0 million.
The contrasting performance comes as Bitcoin struggles to recover from its latest selloff, trading around $64,871 as of press time after briefly approaching $61,000 over the weekend.
BlackRock defies broader Bitcoin ETF selling as market enters negative territory
Despite its recent withdrawal streak, BlackRock remains one of the few major Bitcoin ETF issuers attracting more capital than it has lost this year.
ETF market data showed that IBIT had accumulated approximately $2.10 billion in net inflows during 2026 as of Nov. 13, while the broader market recorded $1.82 billion in net withdrawals.
The divergence is also evident in cumulative flows since launch.
BlackRock's cumulative net inflows reached approximately $64.27 billion following Monday's positive session, exceeding the $54.71 billion attracted by the entire US spot Bitcoin ETF market.
Meanwhile, IBIT held approximately $53.99 billion in assets as of Nov. 13, reflecting the impact of Bitcoin's decline on the fund's market value.
Bloomberg ETF analyst Eric Balchunas highlighted BlackRock's resilience, describing its ability to retain positive inflows despite deteriorating sentiment as remarkable. He said:
“I mean seriously $IBIT is still +$2b net inflows YTD which is unreal given the sentiment and price action.”
However, he acknowledged that Bitcoin remained in a particularly difficult market environment.
Indeed, trading firm Wintermute has identified weakening demand across several sources of capital. For context, the market is currently grappling with a $14 billion to $16 billion contraction in stablecoin supply over 30 days and also weakening demand from corporate Bitcoin treasury buyers.
Wintermute also warned that Bitcoin's recent decline below its 200-week moving average near $68,000 had weakened the market's technical structure. According to the firm:
“It is now clear we haven’t cleared the bear market yet, and the rally off the July low was a fake-out.”
In view of this, the market maker said it remained defensive after approximately $1.7 billion in liquidations over the weekend, arguing that a short-covering-driven rebound would not necessarily signal renewed capital inflows.
Wintermute identified a daily Bitcoin close above $68,000 accompanied by positive ETF flows as one condition that could change its short-term bearish stance.
items.title: BlackRock single-handedly ends Bitcoin ETFs’ $1.9 billion exodus as seven rivals keep bleeding

items.content:
In brief
- Standard Life chairman Sir Nicholas Lyons said tokenized gilts could make it easier for ordinary savers to buy UK government bonds.
- He urged the UK to make its digital gilt pilot a success, build tokenized collateral markets, and ensure retail investors share in the benefits.
- Lyons warned that tokenization does not make investments safer, saying "fractional ownership of a risky asset remains ownership of a risky asset."
Tokenization could help ordinary British savers buy government bonds more easily, and should not become a tool only for big financial institutions, according to Sir Nicholas Lyons, chairman of Standard Life.
"Why should it be so unnecessarily complicated for retail investors to buy gilts that fund the nation's needs?" Lyons said at Solana's Breakpoint conference in London.
Lyons, a former Lord Mayor of the City of London whose company has about £480 billion ($633 billion) in assets under administration, said Britain should use tokenization to bring more households into investing. About £850 billion ($1.1 trillion) of household wealth remains in cash, often losing value to inflation, he said.
Tokenization could cut administrative costs, make transfers simpler and let savers invest in small amounts in products that would otherwise be uneconomic, Lyons said. More retail ownership of gilts would make the UK less reliant on foreign buyers and could help erode the risk premium the country has paid on its debt since the September 2022 mini-budget, he added.
The DIGIT pilot
The remarks come as the UK prepares to issue its first digitally native government bond, known as DIGIT. Earlier this month, the Treasury confirmed roles for six banks supporting the pilot, with issuance expected in the first quarter of 2027, Lyons said.
"Government bonds sit at the heart of our financial system," he said, noting that they underpin liquidity, provide collateral and set reference rates for other assets. Showing that tokenized gilts can be issued, settled and used as collateral efficiently would lay "an important foundation for much broader digital capital markets," he said.
Lyons credited the Financial Conduct Authority, the Bank of England and the Treasury for progress so far, including the Digital Securities Sandbox and work to let tokenized securities be used as collateral.
The Bank of England has also turned its attention to stablecoins: an executive has said it is treating them as a new form of money, it eased its planned stablecoin rules in June, and it has since been handed a legal duty to foster stablecoin innovation. Lyons cited a July report by Chris Woolard, the government's wholesale digital markets champion, which estimated that faster adoption of digital markets could add as much as £33 billion ($43.5 billion) a year to UK economic output by 2035.
But the competition is moving fast, he warned, pointing to the SEC's innovation exemption for tokenized stock trading in the U.S., and initiatives in Europe, Singapore, Hong Kong, Switzerland and the Middle East.
Four priorities
Lyons set out four priorities: making the digital gilt pilot a success, accelerating tokenized collateral and repo markets, promoting interoperability to avoid "a collection of competing digital platforms that recreate the fragmentation of the existing system," and ensuring retail investors share in the benefits.
He also acknowledged the risks, citing concerns raised by the Financial Times' Gillian Tett that AI-accelerated cyber threats and faster-moving money could fuel a run on deposits. "Tokenization does not automatically make an investment safer, more liquid, or more stable, or suitable for retail investors," he said. "Fractional ownership of a risky asset remains ownership of a risky asset."
"We're not pursuing tokenization for the sake of technological leadership," Lyons said. "We're pursuing better capital markets, more productive investment, greater economic prosperity, and wider participation in the creation of wealth and jobs."
