items.author: Oluwapelumi Adejumo
items.content:
Quick Take
- Hyperliquid's weekly trading volume surged 16% to $75.7 billion, even as its USDC holdings fell 7.8% to $6.02 billion.
- The exchange has accumulated $3.37 billion in HYPE burns, with trading fees and USDC reserve income supporting continued token purchases.
- Shrinking USDC balances could weaken reserve income, raising questions about whether trading fees can offset any decline in buyback funding.
Hyperliquid's perpetual futures trading volume surged nearly 16% over the past week, even as the network's USDC holdings declined, exposing competing trends in the revenue streams supporting HYPE token buybacks.
Data from DeFiLlama showed that the decentralized exchange processed $75.72 billion in perpetual futures transactions over the seven days ending Nov. 16, an increase of 15.87%.
However, USDC capitalization on the network fell 7.76% to $6.02 billion during the same period. The stablecoin accounted for approximately 98.85% of Hyperliquid's total stablecoin supply.
The divergence puts Hyperliquid's token-buyback model in focus, particularly as the protocol increasingly relies on both trading fees and income generated from stablecoin reserves to support HYPE purchases.
Hyperliquid has already accumulated about 49.03 million HYPE tokens through its Assistance Fund, representing 4.9% of the cryptocurrency's initial one-billion-token supply.
Under the protocol's rules, the holdings were treated as burned and were valued at about $3.37 billion as of Nov. 17. Their estimated acquisition cost was $1.45 billion, with an average purchase price near $29.50 per token.
How trading activity fuels Hyperliquid's multibillion-dollar HYPE burns
Hyperliquid's fee structure directs trading revenue toward liquidity providers, market deployers, and the Assistance Fund, which automatically converts its allocated fees into HYPE.
The accumulated tokens are permanently removed from the circulating supply, linking exchange activity directly to demand for its native cryptocurrency.
This mechanism has become an important component of HYPE's token economics, with the protocol using revenue from its trading business to steadily accumulate tokens.
The latest increase in perpetuals volume strengthens one side of that arrangement by expanding the trading activity from which fees are collected.
However, the amount reaching the Assistance Fund also depends on transaction fee tiers, staking discounts, maker rebates and revenue-sharing arrangements with market deployers.
Hyperliquid has also expanded its funding model beyond trading fees through AQAv2, an arrangement that redirects income earned on eligible USDC reserves toward the protocol.
Under the framework, Hyperliquid receives approximately 90% of cost-adjusted reserve yield, providing another source of funds for HYPE purchases.
Coinbase serves as the treasury operator, while Circle provides technical support for the stablecoin infrastructure.
Unlike trading fees, which depend on transaction activity, this income is tied to qualifying USDC balances and prevailing interest rates.
That creates a potential vulnerability as stablecoin capitalization declines, even while activity on the exchange strengthens.
Falling USDC balances put reserve income under pressure
The importance of Hyperliquid's stablecoin reserves became more apparent in the third quarter, when the network began generating substantial income through the AQAv2 arrangement.
According to Bitwise and Allium, the protocol accrued approximately $17.26 million in USDC reserve income during the quarter, including $14.86 million in September.
At the end of September, Hyperliquid held approximately $7.35 billion in total USDC, with $6.77 billion backing HyperCore, its trading infrastructure. Of that amount, the treasury held approximately $6.09 billion.
Using those balances and a 3.22% annual reference rate, Bitwise estimated the arrangement could generate about $16.09 million over 30 days, or nearly $196 million annually.
That potential income adds another source of demand for HYPE, reinforcing the buybacks already funded by trading fees.
The latest contraction in USDC capitalization threatens to weaken that contribution if the decline extends to the qualifying reserves on which the income is earned.
The reserve arrangement calculates revenue from daily balances and interest rates over 30-day periods, with payments reaching the Assistance Fund eight days after each period ends.
Consequently, shrinking eligible reserves would gradually reduce the income available for HYPE purchases, while stronger trading activity could help compensate through higher fee collections.
For Hyperliquid, the emerging tension is between an increasingly active derivatives business and a contracting stablecoin base that supports a separate source of buyback funding.
The next reserve-income distribution will provide a clearer picture of whether Hyperliquid can sustain this additional source of HYPE demand as USDC balances fall.
items.title: Hyperliquid’s $3.4 billion HYPE burn machine faces new test as USDC reserves shrink

items.author: Jacob Lyon
items.content:
Star Trek actor William Shatner has called out Pump Fun after he spotted a “fraudulent” Star Trek-themed token promising to send profits to his charity.
Last Friday, Shatner, who played Captain James T. Kirk for almost 30 years across TV and film, first noticed the token in a fake press release posted by Blockzeit last July.
The release claimed that Shatner announced crypto token Quatloos ($QUATS), a name harking back to the currency of an alien planet from Star Trek where gladiators fight to the death.
It even concocted a fake Shatner quote about the evolution of technology and “venturing into the unknown.”
Shatner says he has nothing to do with it, calls out Pump Fun
Shatner, however, claimed he hadn’t authorized anything and described the article’s attempts to promote a token in the name of his charity, Hollywood Charity Horse Show, as “despicable” and a “scam.”
This week Shatner noted, “Of course these scam tokens are on [Pump Fun].” He’s now trying to contact the memecoin platform’s management team and founders Alon Cohen and Sapijiju.
Read more: Pump Fun and Kraken delete Hunter Biden $LAPTOP promotion
The actor argued that whoever’s behind the token “is just stealing the money,” and claimed that the Quatloos name is copyrighted by media conglomerate Skydance.
A call was also made for Blockzeit to remove his name from the article, but it remains up at the time of writing.
Shatner’s charity rejected donation from Pump Fun partner
The CFO of Shatner’s charity also rejected a donation from the founder of a crypto-based charity called Donate.gg this week.
Shatner said, “Your Donation company received those funds under false pretenses which is fraud. I am also requesting that you remove my charity’s page from your website and do not allow anyone to put up a page for it.”
He added, “I don’t care if it’s permissionless. You are helping to participate in fraud and I will not stand for that.”
Leap, the founder of Donate.gg, later removed the charity page. It made the donation while collaborating with Pump Fun on charity coins.
Read more: Pump Fun’s Kimchi partnership has turned into chaos
Shatner called critics ‘crypto-cretins’
Shatner’s donation rejection drew criticism from crypto users, who the actor later described as “crypto-cretins.”
Despite his apparent disdain for crypto, Shatner promoted a media-focused crypto token last year called $BILL that gives buyers access to his one-man show Shatner’s World.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Zoltan Vardai
items.content:
Solana Foundation takes majority interest in crypto data firm CoinGecko
Solana Foundation now holds a majority interest in CoinGecko, its product chief said, as the crypto data platform explores trading features.
Solana Foundation now holds a majority interest in crypto data aggregator CoinGecko, the foundation’s chief product officer, Vibhu Norby, said Tuesday.
CoinGecko announced the backing but did not disclose the financial terms. It said it plans to use it to strengthen its data infrastructure, expand data coverage across tokenized real-world assets and derivatives, and develop onchain trading and market intelligence tools.
The Solana Foundation “now has a majority interest in CoinGecko” and plans to collaborate on developing “new on-platform trading & DeFi experiences with Solana,” Norby said in a Tuesday X post.
CoinGecko said its data methodologies would remain transparent and publicly accessible and that it would continue serving the broader crypto ecosystem. Its website, app and application programming interface, which supplies data to other services, will continue operating as usual.
Founded in 2014, CoinGecko serves an average of over 10 million monthly users and receives over 200 million monthly page views, according to its About page.
Cointelegraph has contacted the Solana Foundation and CoinGecko to ask about the size of the deal, but had not received a response by publication time.

items.author: Aaron Wise
items.content:
Digg founder Kevin Rose has claimed that customers paying thousands of dollars a year to use cloud-based agreement management software Docusign could actually do everything it offers for free.
This week, Rose launched SignuDoc, free, open source code that he claims can deploy in “one click” with “full audit trails, tamper-evident seals and your documents never leave your cloud.”
The post earned about 2 million views in its first day.
Its contributor list includes an entry named “Claude,” including code merged from a branch with “Claude” in its name, so Rose almost certainly used AI to vibe-code parts of his new offering.
An anagram of Docusign, SignuDoc competes with Docusign’s primary value proposition as an e-signature software package that simplifies requesting, emailing, storing, and auditing of PDF signatures.
Despite the viral attention it’s received, Rose’s competitor isn’t the first attempt to clone Docusign software. Moreover, the newcomer lacks critical features, and a former employee claimed that PDF signatures are only a small part of Docusign’s business, anyway.
On Wall Street, investors’ immediate reaction was a shrug. Docusign’s Nasdaq-listed DOCU common stock closed down 1.2%.
Kevin Rose versus Docusign
SignuDoc does, as Rose suggests, execute Docusign’s core PDF signing loop.
It offers white-label branding, dashboards for every document, up to 10 signers per envelope, email-based signing, private Vercel-based storage, and full audit trails with tamper-evident seals.
The project says the free tiers from Vercel, Neon, and Resend cover roughly 250 documents a month. However, a company must already be paying for Vercel Pro at $20 a month to store documents and certificates.
A free version isn’t technically possible without violating Vercel’s terms of service for most users’ commercial purposes. Vercel’s free tier bars commercial use.
Docusign also sells considerable features that Rose’s clone lacks, including bulk sending, web forms, payment collection, a paid API, more than 1,000 integrations, and compliance standards like SOC 2.
Read more: DeFi, meet Claude: Moonwell’s ‘vibe-coded’ oracle in $1.8M blowup
Even Rose’s documentation concedes, “Docusign does more, and charges for it per user. SignuDoc does the everyday signing loop well.”
Another major gap is compliance. Docusign points to SOC 2 Type 2 reports and 21 CFR Part 11 adherence for regulated workflows.
SignuDoc, in contrast, has no SOC 2 report of its own. Its documentation offers a Part 11 mode, with validation entirely left to the customer.
Critics jump into the comment section
The top reply under Rose’s viral post points this out, “No SOC2, no enterprise legal sign-off. Good luck.”
Another asked, “Who’s paying for the certificates for each e-sign?”
Yet another critic replied, asking who will be paying for document envelopes in Rose’s free clone. “Docusign KBA envelopes are super expensive. Mandated by the counterparty.”
DocuSign’s stock trades at a generous 49x trailing earnings multiple. If any software can genuinely compete with its premium offerings, that multiple could certainly shrink.
The company’s latest annual report says e-signature subscriptions were the “substantial majority” of its $3.22 billion in fiscal 2026 revenue.
Many other Docusign clones have come and gone in prior years without displacing Docusign’s market share, including OpenSign, LibreSign, DocuSeal, and Documenso.

items.title: Digg founder Kevin Rose just ‘cloned’ Docusign with AI

items.author: Gino Matos
items.content:
Quick Take
- DBS and Kinexys connected institutional dollar accounts in Singapore and the US, with Ant International as the first client.
- The network runs continuously, while transfers between Kinexys and traditional accounts pause for three hours on Saturdays.
- BIS research supports partial substitution between deposits and stablecoins, while the banks' launch leaves customer savings unquantified.
Singapore bank DBS and JPMorgan's blockchain business Kinexys have connected their blockchain-based dollar accounts in Singapore and the US, allowing institutional clients to transfer funds instantly around the clock as an alternative to stablecoins, according to DBS's Nov. 16 announcement.
The service gives corporate treasurers another way to move bank deposits beyond traditional banking hours.
Ant International is the first client of the commercially ready connection, which uses Partior to coordinate settlement between the banks' permissioned networks. The launch puts a practical service behind the interoperability framework the banks announced in November 2025.
Tokenized deposits as an alternative to stablecoins
The competitive opportunity for banks is to make deposits easier to move while preserving the customer relationship attached to them.
Stablecoins offer another way to transfer dollars digitally, but whether companies favor one route depends on where they can send the money, how they recover cash, and what the whole transaction costs.
A tokenized deposit represents a bank deposit, while USDC is issued by Circle affiliates and backed by cash and cash-equivalent reserves. Moving either on a blockchain does not make the customer's counterparty or redemption arrangements identical.
DBS says transfers within Kinexys's Blockchain Deposit Account network operate 24/7/365. However, moving money between those accounts and traditional demand-deposit accounts has a maintenance interruption every Saturday from 3 p.m. to 6 p.m. Eastern Time.
The banks did not disclose fees or how much cash Ant needs to keep on hand, so companies have no like-for-like cost comparison with stablecoin transfers.
Circle says standard banking-rail USDC redemptions can be free and typically settle in up to two business days, while qualifying Circle Platform and Circle Payments Network customers can obtain free near-real-time redemption.
Circle attributes fast redemption to cash pre-positioned at bank partners, which earns less than Treasuries, and its Mint product terms also make instant settlement conditional on participating banks offering it.
Direct Mint access is restricted to eligible institutions, while individuals obtain USDC through exchanges and wallets.
Deposit rates reveal the competitive stakes
A Bank for International Settlements (BIS) working paper published Oct. 13 uses weekly US data from January 2019 through June 2025. Researchers Rashad Ahmed and Iñaki Aldasoro found that higher deposit rates were followed by slower stablecoin growth, and that the relationship was stronger for USDC than USDT.
The paper links a one-standard-deviation increase in deposit repricing to about 2.4 percentage points slower stablecoin growth over ten weeks. Stablecoin growth averaged 15% over a ten-week period in the sample.
The findings suggest that deposit pricing helps shape demand for stablecoins, but the authors say their analysis does not establish that stablecoin growth necessarily reduces total bank deposits or lending.
The DBS link is part of a wider effort to make bank money usable across more systems, though the products are distinct.
On Oct. 19, JPMorgan brought its JPM Coin deposit token to Ethereum, alongside Base, for institutional clients. That public-chain token is separate from the permissioned Blockchain Deposit Account network connected to DBS.
Using its internal data, JPMorgan reported more than $4 trillion in cumulative transactions and $7 billion in average daily volume across the broader Kinexys platform.
In September, DBS said it and Citi's New York office had completed a dollar payment via SWIFT Digital Ledger in minutes over a weekend.
Separately, The Clearing House selected Quant to support a tokenized-deposit network with connections to RTP and CHIPS. Participating institutions are expected to gain access in the first half of 2027.
A faster transfer inside one network only helps if the receiving bank can accept it.
The competition is consequently about more than whose blockchain runs all weekend. The decisive advantage for corporate cash would be money available where it is needed, with fewer costly balances waiting elsewhere.
items.title: JPMorgan and DBS offer 24/7 dollar transfers… without stablecoins

截至发文时，约 34.5 万美元已被返还，仍有约 18.3 万美元尚未追回。部分涉事用户已主动退还重复收到的资金，也有账户将资金转出至其他链上地址。目前，Relay Protocol 和 Lighter 均未对此事作出回应。相关交易记录均可在 Lighter 区块浏览器中查询。

items.author: Cointelegraph by Yohan Yun
items.content:
Bitcoin to $1M by 2030? ‘Almost certainly not,’ says Dragonfly’s Qureshi
Dragonfly’s Haseeb Qureshi says Bitcoin could reach $400,000 by 2030 but doubts it will return to $100,000 by year-end with the rout in AI stocks weighing on crypto.
Bitcoin is unlikely to reach $1 million by 2030 — though it could reach $400,000 — according to Dragonfly managing partner Haseeb Qureshi.
“The amount of capital that would have to come into crypto to get to million-dollar Bitcoin is an astronomical sum,” Qureshi tells Cointelegraph’s Trade Secrets. “The idea that you could get that amount of capital in five years or four years is just not plausible.”
A former professional poker player and software engineer at Airbnb, Qureshi now backs crypto startups at Dragonfly, which launched a $650 million fund in February.
Qureshi also says he doubts Bitcoin will return to six figures by year-end, linking the current crypto sell-off to the rout in AI stocks.
AI sell-off spills into Bitcoin
Nvidia (NVDA) shares closed 4.3% lower on Thursday after the chipmaker announced co-founder Jensen Huang’s resignation as CEO following a series of scandals. Huang reportedly had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. Beijing denied the espionage allegation and President Donald Trump has expressed doubts too.
Nvidia is the leading AI chip supplier and accounted for 4.66% of the MSCI All Country World Index at the end of October, second only to Apple.
Bitcoin fell alongside Nvidia shares in the week Jensen Huang stepped down as CEO. Source: TradingView
“Crypto is not the main story this year for financial markets,” Qureshi says. “Crypto is downstream of these other stories.”
Qureshi says investors grew concerned after Democrat sweep in the US midterms that new data centers would be harder to get approved. With high oil prices and inflation already weighing on the economy, the prospect of weaker AI investment prompted investors to cut exposure to riskier assets, including Bitcoin, he says.
Related: Jensen Huang weighs Nvidia comeback days after shock exit: FT
That leaves crypto “largely along for the ride” through the year-end.
Crypto has spent much of 2026 in a bear market despite Bitcoin’s 43% recovery in the third quarter. Bitcoin traded near $65,000 on Monday, almost 50% below its October 2025 all-time high.
Bitcoin is far away from its $126,080 all-time high recorded in October 2025. Source: CoinGecko
The US Senate failed to advance the CLARITY Act in September, stalling the industry’s push for federal rules for crypto markets. In October, suspected North Korean hackers stole about $6.3 billion from Binance in the largest crypto theft on record.
Digital gold as a rival to actual gold
Over the next 15 to 20 years, Qureshi says Bitcoin could compete with gold as a store of value outside government control.
New deposits or advances in mining could add to the supply of gold, he says while Bitcoin’s protocol caps its supply at 21 million units.
“There will never be an asteroid that you will find a bunch of Bitcoin on.”
However, Qureshi sees a risk that AI could discover a flaw in the mathematics that secures Bitcoin transactions.
Bitcoin uses digital signatures to verify that a transaction was signed with the corresponding private key. If a future mathematical breakthrough makes it possible to forge those signatures, attackers could move coins without their owners’ permission.
Such a threat is often discussed alongside quantum computing risks. A powerful quantum computer could derive a private key from its corresponding public key using Shor’s algorithim, putting coins with public keys visible at risk of theft, which includes some of Satoshi Nakamoto’s early holdings.
Related: Nearly 10% of Bitcoin supply is ‘structurally unsafe’ from quantum breakthrough: Glassnode
In October, OpenAI said one of its models had found a faster way to solve certain logic problems, challenging a conjecture known as the Exponential Time Hypothesis.
Qureshi says a future AI-assisted discovery could break the cryptography Bitcoin uses to verify who can spend coins, undermining its case as a store of value.
“That, I think, is what you should price in as the chance this all breaks, this all fails,” he says.
Dragonfly’s bets on stablecoins and AI
Dragonfly has a history of backing innovative projects, and led stablecoin project Ethena’s $6 million seed round in 2023. Ethena had about $4.9 billion of its dollar-linked USDe token outstanding at the end of September. The protocol uses derivatives to offset price swings in the assets backing USDe. Some of the income those positions generate goes to users who stake the token.
Dragonfly also led a $65 million funding round for the privacy focused AI firm Venice in July. The startup said it had 3.5 million registered users and put its valuation at $1 billion. Venice says it keeps chat histories on users’ devices and lets them choose among models with different privacy settings.
Users who stake Venice’s VVV token can mint DIEM, which they can stake for daily credits to run AI models.
Qureshi says demand for services like Venice could grow as users look for more privacy and fewer restrictions on what they can ask.
Hodler’s Digest: US sellers drive Bitcoin crash, Jensen plots Nvidia comeback

items.author: Liam 'Akiba' Wright
items.content:
Quick Take
- Treasury’s 10-year real yield reached 2.92% on November 16, even as the nominal yield fell to 5.12%.
- The real-yield increase was one basis point on Monday and 29 basis points across November 6–16.
- Higher real yields can raise Bitcoin’s opportunity cost, but the divergence alone establishes no Bitcoin price response.
The 10-year Treasury yield after inflation rose to 2.92% on Monday, Nov. 16, up 29 basis points since Nov. 6. The move left Bitcoin competing with that yield even as the headline 10-year Treasury rate fell.
Treasury’s nominal yield data showed a decline to 5.12% from 5.15% on Friday, Nov. 13, a three-basis-point move. Its real-yield series moved the other way, edging up one basis point from 2.91%.
The real yield had stood at 2.63% on Nov. 6. The 29-basis-point rise therefore spans multiple sessions, with Monday adding only one basis point.
Why the real yield matters for Bitcoin
Bitcoin provides no contractual interest income. A higher yield on inflation-protected government debt can therefore raise the opportunity cost of holding it: investors have a stronger income alternative against which to weigh Bitcoin’s potential returns and volatility.
The 2.92% figure is also a long-term Treasury curve benchmark, not an overnight borrowing rate or a promised return for every investor. Treasury estimates its constant-maturity nominal and real par yields from indicative market quotations. An investor’s realized return on a particular bond can differ.
A simple subtraction of Treasury’s real par yield from its nominal par yield gives a spread of 2.20 percentage points on Monday, down from 2.24 on Friday. The four-basis-point narrowing explains how the nominal benchmark could fall while the real benchmark rose.
The spread is often described as inflation compensation. But the Federal Reserve’s explanation shows why it cannot be read as a pure inflation forecast: it also reflects compensation for inflation risk and differences in liquidity between nominal Treasuries and inflation-protected securities. The subtraction alone cannot show which component drove Monday’s change.
Historical research supports caution about the transmission to crypto. The authors of a 2023 IMF working paper found that U.S. monetary tightening reduced a broad crypto price factor through investor risk-taking. Their study does not estimate how Monday’s one-basis-point real-yield move affected Bitcoin.
Watch the inflation-adjusted Treasury yield for signs that competition from bonds is easing. The headline rate can fall while that yield stays elevated.
items.title: How Bitcoin still competes with a 2.92% Treasury yield after inflation

英伟达高管：芯片从出厂至系统出货周期可由五周缩至两周，正围绕CPO技术构建新的供应链

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 17 日，英伟达运营执行副总裁 Deb Shoquist 表示，在需要时，英伟达可将芯片从台积电出厂到系统从富士康、纬创出厂的周期，由五周缩短至两周。公司每周根据各工厂的产能及生产表现分配芯片，并对每颗芯片实施从裸片编号到客户发票的全程追踪。

Deb Shoquist 表示，随着英伟达从芯片供应商转向数据中心系统公司，供应链需要覆盖更多技术领域。部分光组件合作伙伴具备技术能力，但缺乏扩产所需的规模和资金，英伟达正通过投资及合作提供支持，并围绕共封装光学（CPO）技术构建新的供应链。

items.content:
ARK sells $85M in Nvidia shares ahead of chipmaker’s Q3 earnings results
ARK bought shares in Block, Circle and Coinbase worth about $39.9 million at Monday’s close while selling Nvidia and Solana and Ether staking ETFs.
Funds managed by Cathie Wood’s ARK Investment Management bought shares in Block, Circle and Coinbase worth about $39.9 million at Monday’s closing prices, while selling Nvidia shares and Solana and Ether staking ETFs.
ARK sold 543,092 Nvidia (NVDA) shares worth approximately $84.8 million and about 30,659 Bullish (BLSH) shares valued at about $605,000. The company also sold about 350,000 shares of 3iQ Solana Staking ETF and 300,000 shares of the 3iQ Ether Staking ETF, according to its Monday trade disclosure.
The funds bought 277,523 Block shares, 180,534 Circle shares and 53,760 Coinbase shares, according to ARK’s Monday trade disclosure. Those purchases were valued at approximately $23 million, $10.4 million and $6.4 million, respectively, using closing prices. ARK also bought 378,515 SpaceX shares, valued at about $52 million.
ARK’s Nvidia sale comes ahead of the chipmaker’s third-quarter earnings results scheduled for publication after market close on Tuesday, which are expected to test whether AI infrastructure spending can justify Nvidia’s growth expectations.
Nvidia earnings follow leadership change
Nvidia’s stock fell 4% on Monday to close at $156, extending its year-to-date decline to over 16%, according to Yahoo Finance data. Nvidia’s shares declined after its board members reportedly ruled out co-founder Jensen Huang’s return as CEO.
Related: Jensen Huang weighs Nvidia comeback days after shock exit: FT
Huang resigned last week following reports of extramarital affairs, one of which was with an alleged Chinese spy, with chief financial officer Colette Kress taking over as interim CEO.
S&P Global Market Intelligence analyst Melissa Otto said the key question is whether the earnings release can provide the “next positive catalyst for the stock or are expectations largely priced in for now,” according to a Thursday report.
The analyst expects Nvidia to report third-quarter revenue of about $109.3 billion, led by $101.8 billion from its data center business.
Nvidia year-to-date chart. Source: Yahoo Finance

Morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner. The analysis and opinions expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Decrypt. And check out our daily news show 'FOMO HOUR' covering all of the top stories and market action.
GM!
Today’s top news:

🏛️ Backpack and tZERO Win the First Onchain Derivatives Approvals
For years, perps were the product American traders couldn’t legally touch. On Monday, that officially changed.
Chairman Michael Selig approved applications from Backpack and tZERO to run regulated derivatives exchanges and clearinghouses that execute and settle on blockchain rails. Selig called it “an important milestone in the evolution of American financial markets.”
Backpack got both pieces at once, a Designated Contract Market designation to run the exchange and a Derivatives Clearing Organization registration to clear its own trades. It plans to offer Americans round-the-clock leveraged crypto perps on a single global order book, accepting both fiat and crypto as collateral with cross-margin across positions. tZERO received its exchange approval a week earlier, after already holding clearing registration, and is building it into a derivatives vertical inside its infrastructure business.
Backpack US president Mark Wetjen, himself a former CFTC commissioner, framed it as “moving price discovery from offshore unregulated venues to the United States.” CEO Armani Ferrante said the firm enters markets “fully regulated from day one.” Backpack already runs licensed platforms in Europe, Asia and the UAE.
The CFTC has certainly been busy this month. They cleared single-stock perpetual futures on November 3. It issued guidance on November 5 telling federally regulated exchanges they generally cannot restrict access by state. Now it has approved blockchain-native exchanges and clearinghouses.
Selig is building an onshore home for every product the offshore venues were built to serve, and he is doing it through staff action rather than legislation, with one sitting commissioner and nomination hearings for two more this week.
So who’s next?
Hyperliquid is the obvious candidate and also the one that has publicly said it doesn’t want this. Jeff Yan spent his Bloomberg interview this month arguing Hyperliquid is infrastructure rather than an exchange, and that regulators should oversee the firms deploying markets on top rather than the chain underneath. His US route is HIP-3 partners taking on the compliance burden, with ICE investing in Trade.xyz and Kraken’s parent reportedly in talks. Backpack getting a DCM and a DCO makes that argument harder, because it demonstrates a crypto-native venue can simply register.
Then there’s Lighter. It has run Robinhood Wallet’s perps since July on a dedicated instance with a 50/50 revenue split, which is the partner model rather than the registration model. The registered model opens up with a CFTC license, and many think Lighter could very well be next.
One thing’s certain—the CFTC is serious about bringing perps onshore. From Selig himself, “I look forward to building on that milestone.” And we will find out soon enough who’s next…

items.author: Decrypt Agent
items.content:
In brief
- Solana Foundation AI lead Rishin Sharma said agents now drive 76% of AI token use on OpenRouter, up from 8% a year earlier.
- The foundation has launched Solana AI, a hub for more than 120 teams building AI products on the network, alongside new payments and privacy tools.
- Macro investor Raoul Pal said AI agents are not yet meaningful economic actors, but will turn to blockchains to pay for things.
AI agents are becoming the internet's main users, and the Solana Foundation wants its blockchain to be how they pay for things.
"The biggest opportunity in crypto is already underway," Rishin Sharma, who leads AI at the Solana Foundation, said at the Breakpoint conference in London.
Sharma used his presentation to showcase Solana.ai, a new homepage for the network's AI ecosystem, which the foundation launched last week. More than 120 teams are now building AI products on Solana across payments, trading and infrastructure, he said.
'Agentic is the new majority'
Bots and other automated software accounted for more than 53% of global web traffic in 2025, up from 51% the year before, according to cybersecurity firm Imperva's latest Bad Bot Report, which Sharma cited. Agents have also come to dominate AI usage: API keys classified as agentic accounted for 76% of the tokens processed through model marketplace OpenRouter in October 2026, up from 8% a year earlier, according to the company's monthly data recap.
At the same time, AI is getting much cheaper. Sharma's slides showed the price of a million tokens falling from $37.50 for GPT-4 to $0.14 for GPT-5 nano, a 270-fold drop, while monthly token use has risen around 330-fold.
"Which model is smarter matters a little bit less, and what matters more is what the model can actually do," Sharma said. "What are the tools it's using? What are the data it's able to access? And what money can it functionally use?"
Paying for the agentic internet
Payments are where that shift is showing up first, Sharma said. The x402 standard, which lets AI agents pay for online services, has processed more than 400 million payments and $100 million in volume, up from zero a year ago, he said. Solana-based BlockRun, which he described as the largest x402 server, has handled more than 60 million transactions in the past two months.
The foundation has also launched payment channels that it says can handle 1 million payments per second, a private AI service offering attested private inference on Solana, and Pay.sh, a server integrating more than 100 APIs that agents can pay for, Sharma said. He added that the foundation is working with companies including Google, Alibaba and ByteDance to let them charge for their AI models through agent payments.
Next, the foundation plans to publish benchmarks for how well AI models perform financial tasks, and to launch an on-ramp that lets users convert cash to stablecoins and hand them to their AI assistants, he said.
Macro investor and Real Vision founder Raoul Pal, speaking earlier at the conference, argued that agents are not yet real economic actors. "They're like kids," he said. "These are young kids who spend nothing on a few sweets and stuff." But as stocks and other assets move onchain, he said, agents will start using blockchains to trade and settle, and "the value accrues to the underlying layer one."
Solana has been building toward this for months. The foundation teamed up with Google Cloud on a stablecoin payments service for AI agents in May, while the x402 Foundation, backed by Coinbase and the Linux Foundation, is developing the payments standard. Franklin Templeton has described agentic AI as a killer use case for crypto.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Isabelle Castro
items.content:
Revolut plans four blockchain-based funds for private markets, chair says
Citing a looming liquidity crunch, Martin Gilbert said blockchain could help bring more liquidity to private markets.
Revolut plans to launch four funds using blockchain to offer fractional investments in illiquid markets, chair Martin Gilbert said Tuesday at Solana’s Breakpoint conference in London.
Blockchain, he explained, would be used to divide funds focused on illiquid markets “into what I would term marketable sizes.”
“If you want to buy a private equity fund on Revolut going forward, when we do launch these funds, you will be able to buy them in fractional amounts.”
The company, which has said it has over 80 million customers worldwide, launched a private market investment platform to eligible customers in Europe in July. Managed by a number of firms including Apollo, Ares, Hamilton Lane and Partners Group, the funds already on the platform allow for a minimum investment of 1 euro.
Warning that the financial sector may be entering into a liquidity crunch, particularly in private markets, he highlighted the need to attract more buyers to these markets, which blockchains could facilitate.
“In this world, there is liquidity until there is no liquidity,” he said. “If you can help people get liquidity in illiquid assets, you’re going to solve a lot of problems for a lot of people. The only way you can do that is to be blockchain enabled.”
The company hasn’t yet released details on the blockchain-based funds or when they will launch.

items.title: Lighter reopens withdrawals after trader’s API key leak, returns about $5 million in USDC

items.author: Gino Matos
items.content:
Quick Take
- Lighter restored withdrawals after recovering about $5 million USDC following an attack involving compromised API signing keys.
- The incident highlights how hackers could exploit trading permissions to destroy collateral even without direct withdrawal access.
- Hyperliquid's massive derivatives market raises questions about whether its agent safeguards can contain losses before they reach liquidity providers.
Lighter's Nov. 16 security update described how exposed trading keys enabled an account drain through public-pool shares, putting a potential Hyperliquid exploit in perspective.
Lighter said that withdrawals had resumed after its safeguard allowed about 5 million USDC to be returned.
Hyperliquid has roughly $5.7 billion in open interest, representing about 55% of the open interest in the DefiLlama ranking as of Nov. 16.
Depending on the account permissions, a compromised agent could cause losses through unauthorized orders and liquidation in the accounts it can trade. Wider losses would depend on the affected positions, liquidity providers, and market depth.
Trading authority reaches beyond direct withdrawals
Lighter said that affected accounts used unsafe signing code outside its official software kits. Reused cryptographic signing nonces allowed the attacker to reconstruct API private keys from public signatures, while the protocol, contracts, infrastructure, and official kits were unaffected.
The attacker created a public pool under the affected account, acquired shares through another account, then moved victim funds into the pool without creating corresponding shares. Redeeming the existing shares allowed funds to leave.
The account said wallet signatures were now required for public-pool transfers and that API signatures had been made non-public, with IP allowlists and configurable limits added as further protections.
Separately, Bitquery traced a 10,393,057 USDC withdrawal from Lighter's Ethereum contract on the same day. Its investigation could not inspect the internal rollup transactions or independently establish the reported second account loss.
Hyperliquid's API-wallet documentation says a master account can authorize agents to sign for itself or its subaccounts. Its official agent example describes trading authority without transfer or withdrawal permissions.
The exchange endpoint allows an agent-signed asset transfer when the destination matches the source address, an expressly permitted internal movement distinct from sending assets to another owner.
Hyperliquid also documents a vault-transfer function, and its official Python SDK uses a different signing path for it than for external USDC transfers and bridge withdrawals. The signing code alone does not establish which agent the exchange will authorize to request the exchange.
The derivatives venue's current overview describes customizable HyperEVM accounting and agent delegation, separately from legacy HyperCore vaults. Those distinctions prevent a blanket conclusion about every vault.
A comparable Lighter extraction would require both the relevant permissions and a matching share-accounting path. The documented internal transfers and vault functions leave no basis for a blanket assurance that every agent-authorized vault path is impossible.
A stolen agent with valid authority could open unwanted positions, change exposure, or cause adverse execution. The resulting losses could exhaust the affected account's collateral through trading and liquidation, without a withdrawal to the thief.
Hyperliquid raises the liquidity stakes
The Nov. 16 snapshot showed Hyperliquid open interest of $5.7 billion, against nearly $554 million for Lighter and a tracked total of roughly $10.5 billion. Hyperliquid was about 10.3 times Lighter's size on that measure and accounted for approximately 54.7% of the total.
DefiLlama's Hyperliquid and Lighter protocol pages reported the following activity and bridge snapshots on Nov. 16:
| Measure | Hyperliquid | Lighter | 
|---|---|---|
| Open interest, ranking snapshot | $5.715 billion | $553.97 million | 
| Reported 24-hour perpetual volume | $9.739 billion | $3.710 billion | 
| Bridge headline Total Value Locked (TVL) | $5.694 billion | $491.07 million | 
The first layer of a hypothetical agent compromise is the authorized account. The next layer appears if that account supplies substantial market liquidity: missing quotes or forced hedging could worsen execution for others. HLP losses would require relevant strategy or liquidation exposure.
Market depth also matters more than a venue-wide balance. DefiLlama's exchange snapshot showed about $1.4 billion of aggregate dollar-perpetual depth within 2%, with far less available in individual markets.
Cross-venue effects could develop through shared intermediaries, hedges, and collateral needs, but those connections would have to be established for the affected participants. Lighter's incident does not demonstrate that chain of events at Hyperliquid.
Hyperliquid's earlier episodes illustrate why a trader's loss, a vault drawdown and a platform interruption need separate treatment.
Hyperliquid's history shows who can bear the loss
On March 12, 2025, approximately $4 million in HLP losses followed a large ETH liquidation, leading Hyperliquid to subsequently reduce maximum Bitcoin and Ethereum leverage to 40 times and 25 times.
The March 26 JELLY episode led to a reported loss of nearly $12 million and a later operator statement putting 24-hour HLP profit at roughly 700,000 USDC. As a response, validators delisted the market after suspicious activity.
There was also a November 2025 POPCAT incident that culminated in an estimated $4.9 million HLP loss and a temporary Arbitrum-bridge pause. The fourth episode happened on April 9, with an approximately $1.5 million daily HLP drawdown amid suspected FARTCOIN manipulation.
HLP's <terms state that the community shares the strategy's profit and loss, with withdrawals subject to a four-day delay from the latest deposit. DefiLlama's Nov. 16 HLP snapshot put its headline total value locked (TVL) near $151.9 million.
The clearest documented compensation process followed the July 29, 2025 API disruption. Hyperliquid's Aug. 4 announcement described 37 minutes of delayed orders and error responses even as transactions reached blocks, and its refund method covered specified fills and unusually high funding payments.
The process excluded the smallest calculated refunds and required business or identity verification for larger recipients to receive their full balance.
An Aug. 5 update said refunds had been distributed, describing a conditional response to one operational incident.
How LIT and HYPE reacted
Lighter's token LIT weakened during the incident, dropping from $2.75 to $2.32 right after it, but recovering to $2.88 as of press time
A historical HYPE comparison from 2025 shows the token fell from $14.04 to $12.84 during the March 12 ETH-whale episode, before some recovery.
Relevant escalation signals for Hyperliquid would include an affected account's trading authority and positions, deterioration in the markets it supports, losses reaching HLP, or disruption to settlement and withdrawals.
Its $5.7 billion in open bets makes those distinctions consequential, but the dollar amount threatened by a particular compromise would still depend on the permissions, exposure, and liquidity involved.
items.title: Lighter’s exploit raises uncomfortable questions for Hyperliquid’s $5.7 billion market

Real Vision创始人：区块链将重塑全球金融体系，代币化趋势正在形成

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 17 日，Real Vision 联合创始人兼首席执行官 Raoul Pal 在 Solana Breakpoint 大会上表示，「整个金融体系都将逐步转移到区块链上。Solana 生态已经展示了这一趋势：其规模在 14 至 15 个月内从 1000 万美元增长至 20 亿美元，而且这一过程相当平稳。可以预见，整个金融体系都将逐步吸收并迁移至链上。这也是我早在 2014 年就曾谈及的趋势，如今终于开始成为现实，金融市场正在走向代币化。

这也是我们消除区块空间过剩需求的契机。AI 智能体将作为经济参与者加入这一体系，不断推动链上经济活动发展，并使这一市场的增长空间变得近乎无限。这将成为推动我们在 2034 至 2035 年实现 100 万亿美元规模目标的路径之一。

如今，这一领域还只是一个相对有限的市场，但随着区块空间的使用量不断增长，以及更多具有重要经济价值的基础设施和业务在其上构建，整个 GDP 的计算逻辑也将发生变化。很多人尚未理解这一点，他们仍将区块链视为一种收入型基础设施或工具，但实际上，其潜在市场规模和经济影响远不止于此。」

items.author: Jake Harrison
items.content:
Some of the world’s most popular websites, including CNN, BBC, Fox News and Zoom, were yesterday reportedly serving visitors a malicious package dubbed “OPTIMJACK,” which aims to steal crypto and card details.
By compromising popular website content management tool Optimizely, attackers have been able to inject malicious JavaScript into websites that use the tool, targeting their visitors.
OPTIMJACK was flagged by security researcher Scott Helme, who claimed to have identified 186 affected “high value websites,” noting that “crypto users were the likely target based on the malware.”
In addition to the aforementioned examples, the affected websites also included Ledger, HSBC, IKEA, Salesforce, Air France and GitLab.
Read more: US seizes $1.2 billion frozen after North Korean Binance hack
Helme went on to trace around $7,000 in crypto collected by the scheme, but said that, by approximately 10pm UTC, only one “infected” file remained to be fixed.
Galaxy Research’s Alex Thorn, however, suspects that only around $2,300 is victims’ money, with the remainder being the hacker’s own funds.
Another independent security researcher, Amirul Iman, published a preliminary analysis on his blog, detailing the four elements of the malicious script.
Pasted crypto addresses are replaced, card details skimmed, web cookies and screenshots are sent to the attackers. For iOS users, further material is injected, identified by Helme as the “Coruna and DarkSword exploit kits.”
Iman estimates that up to 1.4 million devices may have been affected by the malware.
Optimizely says it has “identified and contained a security incident affecting some Optimizely Web Experimentation customers” and has reassured users that “the vulnerable path is blocked, the injected code was removed, and customers have been contacted directly.”

items.author: Cointelegraph by Ezra Reguerra
items.content:
US senators seek SEC answers on tokenized stock money laundering risks
Four Democratic senators asked who would be responsible for tokenized shares transferred outside regulated platforms and whether the SEC could freeze or recover those tokens.
Four Democratic senators pressed the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to clarify financial crime safeguards under its tokenized stock exemption, warning that tokenized shares bought by verified investors could reach offshore or unverified wallets.
In a letter released Monday, Senators Angela Alsobrooks, Catherine Cortez Masto, Mark Warner and Ruben Gallego questioned how Anti-Money Laundering and Know Your Customer rules apply to tokenized securities venues, which can trade certain US stocks without registering as securities exchanges.
The senators said the SEC’s Sept. 17 Innovation Exemption requires venues to control trading access but does not mandate restrictions on subsequent transfers. They asked who would be responsible for tokens moved outside of regulated platforms and whether the SEC could recover or freeze them.
The lawmakers also questioned issuers’ rights to object, retail investors’ access to best execution protections and custody safeguards. They asked SEC Chair Paul Atkins 13 questions, urging more transparent rulemaking and requesting answers within 30 days.
When announcing the exemption in September, Atkins said federal anti-fraud and anti-manipulation rules would continue to apply in full.
OKXICE, a venture between crypto exchange OKX and New York Stock Exchange parent Intercontinental Exchange, has also faced issuer objections. Its Nov. 5 public notice listed 67 companies that objected to their tokenized shares being traded on the venue.
Backpack wins CFTC approval for blockchain-based derivatives exchange
Separately, crypto exchange Backpack said Monday that it had secured Commodity Futures Trading Commission approval to establish a US derivatives exchange and clearinghouse using blockchain infrastructure, paving the way for leveraged crypto perpetual futures trading.
CFTC Chair Michael Selig said blockchain-based operators must meet the same regulatory standards as traditional firms, including AML, customer protection and market surveillance requirements.
Backpack also has a tokenized equities business, although its latest CFTC approvals concern derivatives rather than the SEC exemption questioned by lawmakers.
Related: Trump nominates Hester Peirce successor among SEC, CFTC picks
items.title: US senators seek SEC answers on tokenized stock money laundering risks

items.author: Cointelegraph by Helen Partz
items.content:
BlackRock’s Bitcoin ETF snaps $2.35B outflow streak amid extreme fear
BlackRock’s Bitcoin ETF ended 11 sessions of withdrawals totaling $2.35 billion, but CryptoQuant says one day of inflows is too early to signal a recovery.
BlackRock’s spot Bitcoin exchange-traded fund (ETF) returned to inflows Monday, ending an 11-session outflow streak totaling roughly $2.35 billion.
The iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) attracted $76.5 million on Nov. 16, helping US spot Bitcoin ETFs record $7.9 million in net inflows despite withdrawals from several other funds, according to Farside Investors data.
The inflows came as Bitcoin (BTC) traded near multimonth lows of $64,000, while the Crypto Fear and Greed Index, which tracks cryptocurrency market sentiment, fell to 10 out of 100 on Monday, its lowest reading since June 2026.
Nick Pitto, head of marketing at blockchain analytics company CryptoQuant, cautioned against interpreting the inflows as a broader market recovery.
“One day of inflows doesn’t change the picture too much,” Pitto said. He noted that Monday’s inflows recovered only about 3% of IBIT’s withdrawals over the previous 11 sessions, while US Bitcoin ETFs had shed more than 31,000 BTC over the past month.
“It’s too early to call this dip buying,” he said, adding: “We’d need to see several days of inflows in a row, and from more funds than just BlackRock’s.”
Salman Parcy, managing partner at crypto investment company Cequire Capital, offered a more optimistic interpretation, suggesting that some institutional investors may see Bitcoin’s recent decline as a buying opportunity.
“While it is still early to call this a reversal, the return of capital to IBIT does show that some institutional investors are beginning to see an opportunity in current price levels,” Parcy said.
Related: Bitcoin price fails to hold $65K as US stocks drop further on AI nerves
Monday also marked the deadline for most institutions to file their third-quarter Form 13F disclosures, revealing Bitcoin ETF holdings as of Sept. 30. Several institutions reported increased exposure during the quarter, but Pitto cautioned against linking those holdings to Monday’s inflows.
“ETF buying peaked in August and September. But the filings only show what they held at the end of September, not what they’ve done since. So they may not explain Monday’s inflow,” he said.

items.author: Cointelegraph by William Suberg
items.content:
Bitcoin realized loss metric beats June high as open interest eyes 2-year low
Bitcoin short-term holders’ onchain spending notched the largest proportion of realized losses since February after BTC/USD dropped to $62,000.
Bitcoin investors are showing increasing signs of panic as newer buyers’ onchain losses hit their highest since February.
Key points:
- The spent output profit ratio (SOPR) for Bitcoin (BTC) wallets holding for up to 155 days reached 0.955, reflecting the largest realized losses in over nine months.
- SOPR set lower lows than its 0.985 reading from June 30, 24 hours before BTC/USD fell to multiyear lows of $57,800.
- Bitcoin open interest has fallen to $20.498 billion, its lowest level since late 2024, per data from CryptoQuant.
Bitcoin short-term holder onchain losses highest in nine months
Data from onchain analytics platform CryptoQuant reveals new nine-month lows in the spent output profit ratio (SOPR) of Bitcoin’s short-term holders (STH).
SOPR measures the ratio of BTC moving onchain at a higher or lower price relative to the last time it was used in a UTXO. The metric can be broken down by investor cohort, only accounting for coins owned by older or newer hodlers. The latter cohort traditionally consists of speculative entities who are more sensitive to BTC price volatility. An STH entity is a wallet holding a given unit of BTC for up to 155 days without selling.
On Nov. 16, STH-SOPR recorded a reading of 0.955, its lowest since Feb. 7. Readings below 1 reflect STH coins moving onchain on aggregate at a lower price compared to their previous transaction.
Bitcoin STH-SOPR. Source: CryptoQuant
Noticeable deviations below 1 on STH-SOPR imply increased loss-making selling activity by the STH cohort. While BTC/USD briefly dipped to $62,000 this week, the latest reading is notably lower than in late June, when investors reacted to price hitting 20-month lows of $58,534 and STH-SOPR reached 0.985.
In its latest analysis released on Monday, Bitfinex Alpha, the research arm of crypto exchange Bitfinex, noted that in both June and July, swing lows on STH-SOPR corresponded to the “days of heaviest loss-taking” among speculators.
“Net realised losses across all holders reached about 76,500 BTC on 15 November, the largest since 1 July, a significant increase from about 18,700 BTC on 10 November,” it reported.
Bitcoin STH profitability comparison. Source: Bitfinex
Bitfinex added that unrealized losses reveal the pain levels of the broader Bitcoin investor base, with the share of the BTC supply held at loss reaching 48.5% on Nov. 14 — the same as on July 1, when BTC/USD set a new multiyear floor of $57,800.
“Holders are therefore under as much pressure as they were at that low, with price about 11 percent higher,” it wrote.
“Stress of this kind has been necessary for a durable low to form, but the timing is not exact. In June, STH-SOPR fell to these levels four weeks before the low eventually arrived. The signal to watch is a recovery in STH-SOPR toward 1, which would indicate that loss-driven selling is fading.”
BTC price drop sends open interest to 2024 levels
Speculative Bitcoin trading activity overall has witnessed a marked drop in recent weeks.
Related: BTC price tags 18-week low into Nvidia earnings: Three things to know in Bitcoin this week
Open interest, the total number of active derivative positions, dropped to $20.498 billion on Tuesday, a level not seen since late 2024, as measured by CryptoQuant.
Bitcoin OI data. Source: CryptoQuant
In commentary on Monday, CryptoQuant contributor Baykuş flagged a conspicuous drop in OI on Binance as BTC/USD fell from $74,000 to $64,000.
“Open interest on coin-margined BTC-USD contracts fell from $1.55B to $1.1B, and since these contracts are USD-denominated, this reflects real position closures,” they wrote in a blog post.

In brief
- An attacker exploited a flaw in Optimizely's website testing service to inject malware into scripts used by 178 organizations, including Ledger, Zoom and the BBC.
- The code swapped any crypto wallet address on a page or clipboard for the attacker's, and the attacker's wallets received about $7,150 before being emptied.
- Optimizely said it has fixed the vulnerability and removed the code, while researchers urged visitors to check any crypto transfers made on November 16.
An attacker hijacked Optimizely, a platform widely used by companies to run experiments on their websites, to serve malware that swapped visitors' crypto wallet addresses for their own, on sites including hardware wallet maker Ledger.
Optimizely said in a status update on Monday evening that an unauthorized party had exploited a vulnerability in its Experimentation product to add malicious JavaScript to some customer projects. The company said it had fixed the flaw, removed the injected code, secured affected user accounts and added protections to stop unauthorized code being delivered.
Earlier today, Optimizely identified and contained a security incident affecting some Optimizely Web Experimentation customers. The vulnerable path is blocked, the injected code was removed, and customers have been contacted directly.
Updates: https://t.co/ptZHZviIeC
— Optimizely (@Optimizely) November 17, 2026
Researchers at security firm Report URI, which sells tools to detect malicious website scripts, found the malicious code in 188 of the 1,611 Optimizely scripts they examined, belonging to 178 organizations, according to a blog post by founder Scott Helme. The affected sites included Zoom, the BBC, CNN, Salesforce, GitLab, IKEA and HSBC, as well as crypto and trading firms such as Ledger, IG and OANDA.
Because the code was served from Optimizely's own trusted servers, affected websites loaded it without their own systems being breached.
Swapping wallet addresses
The malware's main purpose was to steal crypto. The script scanned web pages for valid wallet addresses on networks including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Tron, Solana and TON, and replaced them with addresses controlled by the attacker, according to Report URI. It also swapped addresses copied to a user's clipboard, meaning anyone who copied an address while an affected page was open could have pasted the attacker's instead.
The attacker's wallets received about $7,150 in crypto, mostly in Bitcoin, Litecoin and USDT, according to Report URI's update on Tuesday. The attacker emptied the wallets early on Tuesday. One Tron address used to cash out had also been used in earlier operations in March and on November 3, allowing Report URI to link the attacker to other attacks, the firm said.
ETH price on November 22, 4:59PM UTC
The script also skimmed card details typed into some sites' own payment forms, though not those entered into hosted payment fields such as Stripe's, and on iPhones and iPads it attempted to load exploit kits known as Coruna and DarkSword, which target older versions of iOS. Report URI said it could not see how many card numbers were stolen or how many devices were compromised.
The injected code first appeared early on November 16 UTC, and had been removed from all of the scripts Report URI could find by late that evening.
How it happened
Optimizely spokesperson Victoria Johnson told Gizmodo that an unauthorized party had "exploited a vulnerability in the Experimentation account signup flow," and that the company had blocked access to the vulnerable path, deployed a fix and notified all affected customers. The company has not said how the attacker gained access to other customers' projects.
Helme said visitors to affected sites on November 16 should check any crypto transfers they made, update their iPhones and iPads, and watch their card statements. Website operators should review custom code in their Optimizely projects and rotate credentials, he added.

谷歌拆分Gemini隐私开关：聊天可以不用于训练，但仍可能被人工查看

动察 Beating AI 快讯，谷歌宣布调整 Gemini 隐私设置。用户终于可以保留聊天记录，同时拒绝让自己的对话用于训练 AI 模型。之前这两个功能被绑在同一个开关上，用户想阻止谷歌拿聊天数据训练模型，就必须同时放弃历史记录。

新设置将聊天历史与模型训练拆开。用户可以分别控制是否保存聊天，以及是否允许谷歌使用聊天文本、上传的文件和图片等内容训练模型。关闭训练授权后，今后的对话原则上不会用于生成式 AI 模型训练，但主动提交反馈的情况除外。

谷歌还延长了关闭聊天历史后的数据保存时间，从原来的最多 72 小时增加到约 2 个月。官方解释是，这些数据仍需用于处理用户请求、反馈和安全问题。

即使禁止将对话用于模型训练，谷歌仍可能出于安全审查和服务改进目的，让人工查看部分聊天内容。经过人工审核的记录会与用户账号分离，最长保存 3 年。即使用户删除聊天历史，这部分记录也不一定会被清除。

新设置将在未来几周陆续向全球用户开放。此前已经关闭「保留活动记录」的用户，迁移后聊天历史和模型训练两个开关都会保持关闭。

items.author: Oluwapelumi Adejumo
items.content:
Quick Take
- Researchers uncovered 188 infected website scripts linked to 178 organizations, including Ledger, in a widespread malware campaign.
- The attack exploited trusted website software to hijack crypto payments, steal card information and potentially target vulnerable iPhones.
- Despite a major cleanup, embedded malware and unanswered questions about the initial breach leave the campaign's full impact uncertain.
Ledger's website was among 178 organizations exposed to malicious scripts that could redirect cryptocurrency payments to hackers, researchers reported Monday.
Cybersecurity firm Report URI discovered the malware in 188 website scripts associated with major brands, including Ledger, BBC, CNN, Zoom, Salesforce and HSBC.
The firm examined 1,611 scripts delivered through Optimizely, a platform businesses use to test and personalize their websites. Attackers had inserted malicious instructions into customer-specific JavaScript, allowing infected code to reach visitors through a service those websites already trusted.
The attack exposed a vulnerability for cryptocurrency users: hackers could redirect funds without stealing private keys or compromising wallets.
Ledger's inclusion in the affected websites does not establish that its hardware wallets, firmware, or signing infrastructure were breached.
How hackers hijacked crypto payments without stealing private keys
The malicious code was designed to identify crypto addresses displayed on websites and replace them with destinations controlled by attackers.
Researchers at Hudson Rock found that the malware could alter wallet addresses in visible text, input fields, links, and clipboard operations. It supported multiple blockchain networks, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, Tron, and Litecoin.
For example, a user copying a legitimate Bitcoin payment address from an infected page could unknowingly paste an attacker-controlled address into their wallet application.
If the user then approved the transaction without verifying the destination, the funds would go to the attacker.
The technique circumvents an important layer of cryptocurrency security because the wallet can function exactly as intended while authorizing a payment to the wrong recipient.
Hudson Rock found no evidence that the recovered malware directly extracted wallet seed phrases or initiated unauthorized blockchain transactions through wallet-signing functions.
However, the attack appears to have generated financial proceeds.
Report URI identified approximately $7,040 received by attacker-linked crypto addresses as of 19:25 UTC on Nov. 16. Bitcoin accounted for roughly $5,380, while additional transactions involved Litecoin, Tron, Ethereum, and BNB Smart Chain.
Beyond cryptocurrency theft, the malware included additional capabilities to intercept payment card information, collect browser-accessible cookies, and capture screenshots.
Researchers also identified code associated with the Coruna and DarkSword iPhone exploit kits, potentially exposing visitors using vulnerable Apple devices to additional attacks.
These capabilities expanded the threat beyond crypto holders to customers interacting with infected websites.
Report URI said a large-scale cleanup reduced the number of infected scripts in its sample from 169 at 20:56 UTC to just one at 21:52 UTC on Nov. 16. Ledger's affected script was reportedly cleaned at approximately 20:41 UTC.
However, the researchers also discovered embedded copies of the malicious code, meaning blocking the attackers' remote servers alone might not eliminate every infection.
The central mystery is how the attackers got permission to modify scripts for so many unrelated organizations.
The researchers have not established whether the intrusion originated from compromised credentials, an Optimizely system, or another access route.
At publication, the investigation had not established the number of affected visitors or the full extent of financial losses, leaving the attackers' initial access method and the campaign's ultimate impact unresolved.
items.title: Hackers found a way to steal crypto without hacking wallets, and Ledger was caught in the attack

Dreamteam融资5300万美元，靠AI自动管理客户，已开始替代Salesforce

动察 Beating AI 快讯，三名美国企业软件公司 Freshworks 前高管创立的 AI 初创公司 Dreamteam 宣布完成累计 5300 万美元融资，投资方包括 Accel、Together Fund 和 Premji Invest。它想用 AI 重新打造企业客户管理软件（CRM），直接挑战 Salesforce 和 HubSpot。

传统 CRM 需要销售人员手动记录客户信息、更新订单进度。Dreamteam 则让 AI 自动读取邮件、会议和客户对话，记住客户提出的要求、价格顾虑以及竞争对手的信息，再持续更新销售记录。

这些信息统一保存在名为 Company Brain 的系统中，供四个 AI 智能体使用。它们分别负责客户调研、会议准备与邮件跟进、销售预测和风险监控，以及 CRM 系统配置。销售人员可以直接用自然语言提出需求，但对外发送的邮件仍需人工批准。

Dreamteam 创始人向 TechCrunch 透露，产品正式销售仅三个月，就在 13 个国家获得超过 100 家企业客户，其中大多数已经付费。医疗企业 DMS Health 已用它替换 Salesforce，流媒体公司 Plex 的广告销售团队也选择了 Dreamteam，而非 HubSpot。

AI 原生 CRM 已经出现多家竞争者。今年 9 月，另一家初创公司 Lightfield 获得 4700 万美元 A 轮融资，同样主打自动记录客户沟通、由 AI 执行销售任务。Salesforce 自己也已推出 AI 智能体，支持自动记录销售活动、准备会议和起草邮件。

--- Top Comments ---

[OtherShrezzing]: This article feels like the result of having unlimited tokens at your disposal. It’s got some very expensive practices, where near-free practices would produce the same or better results. There’s a long section in the middle where the article describes per-change verification via skill files and “ask Claude to use the chrome-for-Claude tool” when checking if changes have introduced regressions. But there’s already tools which do this without spending tokens tokens. Playwright will achieve equ...

[tshaddox]: Is Claude Code considered to be a reliable piece of software these days? I stopped using as my daily driver around 9 months ago, and at that time it felt very heavy/janky and seemed to have very regular bugs and breaking UI changes. I’d be happy to hear that it has gotten better!

[girvo]: > With them, you can run dozens or hundreds in parallel. Im already spending my $2k usd per month in tokens with just one or two agents. How do they expect me to do that?

[Narann]: The more I read articles like this, the more I realize Claude is good for process prototyping, but you need to "bake" the process with flat code/script/organization to decrease costs. The future of IA would actually be to large scale prototype easily, even more like Python was a prototype language.

[koolba]: > Nobody can read every change, so we use failures as one way to decide what needs a person. Whether a human can or should review every diff is a conscious project level decision. I have yet to see a project where it is not feasible. The trick is to break things into small enough pieces that you can review them. Just like one would do if you were doing such changes manually. Nobody in their right mind performs non-mechanical changes of 100s of files.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Zoltan Vardai
items.content:
Google says hackers use AI agents to find and exploit software flaws
Google says attackers are using AI agents to find and exploit software flaws automatically, reducing the time organizations have to apply patches.
Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) said it had, for the first time, identified attackers using AI large language model (LLM) frameworks to automate software vulnerability discovery and exploitation without step-by-step human direction.
In a report published Monday, the researchers described a tool found on an exposed staging server that compared software versions, identified potential flaws, and generated and executed exploit code.
“In the past quarter, GTIG identified threat actors using LLM frameworks to fully automate vulnerability discovery and exploitation without a human in the loop for the first time,” the researchers said.
GTIG identified an exposed staging server hosting a multi-agent vulnerability research and weaponization framework, set up to conduct continuous differential analysis comparing code before and after patch announcements on popular web applications. The model would autonomously discover and exploit software vulnerabilities.
Google warned that these automated workflows give organizations less time to apply security patches before attackers develop ways to exploit vulnerable systems.
In its September report, GTIG said it had “not yet observed threat actors deploying fully autonomous pipelines against targets in the wild.”
Evolution of threat actors using LLMs for exploits. Source: Google
AI agents shorten patching windows
Attackers are leveraging AI agent frameworks to automate patch reverse engineering via differential analysis and weaponizing N-day vulnerabilities, publicly known security flaws.
The report warned that LLMs are enabling attackers to scale “exploitation pipelines against internet-facing servers without human intervention.”
Vulnerability disclosures more than doubled between January and August, according to Google. The number of zero-day vulnerabilities exploited averaged eight per month in 2025 and 11 per month from January through August 2026, reaching 22 in August.
Count of vulnerabilities exploited, by n-days and zero-days, January 2025 to August 2026. Source: Google
These automated workflows also accelerate attackers’ ability to move from initial access to gaining domain administrator access. The report cited an August 2026 PaperCut campaign in which attackers achieved that level of control within minutes, according to cybersecurity firm GreyNoise.
Related: PHP flaw shows AI ‘vulnerability apocalypse’ is on schedule: Immunefi CEO
Cloudflare also reported attempts to exploit the PHP flaws against its customers in October. GTIG said that the two PHP vulnerabilities involved in the exploitation attempts were discovered using LLM analysis, as technical information published before the Oct. 21 patch enabled researchers and attackers to study vulnerabilities and attempt exploits, according to the report.
AI company Anthropic also warned that AI-assisted attacks have evolved into multi-agent operations automating most of the cyberattack cycle from discovery to exploitation and data theft, in a September report.
Anthropic described threat actors running “multi-victim campaigns using agentic AI that would previously have required teams of operators.”
Magazine: How a ‘Wrong Number’ message turned into a $3.4M crypto scam
items.title: Google says hackers use AI agents to find and exploit software flaws

items.content:
In brief
- Nvidia's board is not considering bringing Jensen Huang back as CEO and is focused on its investigation into his conduct, a source told CNBC.
- The report comes as U.S. President Donald Trump said he would welcome Huang's return, and a petition backed by Elon Musk drew nearly 192,000 signatures.
- Nvidia is choosing a search firm to find a permanent CEO, with interim chief Colette Kress set to lead Tuesday's earnings call.
Nvidia's board is not considering bringing back Jensen Huang as CEO, despite a growing campaign for his return led by some of the biggest names in tech and backed by President Donald Trump.
The board is focused on its investigation into Huang and is not in discussions to reinstate him, a person familiar with the matter told CNBC on Monday. The independent investigation, led by law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz, is examining Huang's conduct and whether it compromised national security or company secrets.
Huang resigned as Nvidia's CEO on Thursday, after 33 years at the helm of the company he co-founded. His departure followed his admission of an affair and reports that he had been romantically involved with Alice Huang, an executive at an Nvidia customer whom U.S. officials suspect of spying for China, as well as with Nvidia employees. The week of revelations saw hundreds of billions of dollars wiped from Nvidia's market value.
Calls for a comeback
The report cuts against a weekend of growing pressure for Huang's return. The Financial Times reported that Huang had discussed a comeback with allies, though Altimeter Capital's Brad Gerstner, one of the investors urging the board to keep "all options" open, told CNBC that Huang had not discussed returning with him. A representative for Huang declined to comment on the speculation.
An online petition calling for Huang's reinstatement had drawn 191,996 signatures by Monday. Its backers include Elon Musk, who said on Friday that he was signing it, as well as Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney. The site notes that signatories' affiliations are self-reported and unverified. Nvidia employees have also pushed internally for his return.
Trump said on Monday that he would welcome Huang back. "I would certainly not mind seeing that," he told reporters, adding that national security had not been put at risk, as Decrypt reported. That puts him at odds with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who said on Sunday that Nvidia should look outside the company for its next CEO.
Others in tech have stopped short of backing a return. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, who was briefly ousted from his own company in 2023, said at a Semafor conference on Monday that Huang had "long been a hero of mine," but that he did not know enough to say whether Huang should come back.
Nvidia shares closed down 4.1% at $156.14 on Monday, and were down a further 0.5% at $155.67 in premarket trading early on Tuesday, according to Yahoo! Finance data.
Nvidia's board said on Friday that it was in the process of selecting a search firm for the CEO role. Chief financial officer Colette Kress, the interim CEO, will lead the company's quarterly earnings call on Tuesday.

小AI指挥旧模型，竟在科研任务中打败GPT-5：斯坦福教授创办Noeri获投1.1亿美元

动察 Beating AI 快讯，斯坦福大学两位顶尖 AI 教授 Yejin Choi 和 Carlos Guestrin 创办的 AI 公司 Noeri 正式亮相，并宣布获得 1.1 亿美元融资。Menlo Ventures 领投，英伟达、思科、Snowflake 等参投。

两位创始人都大有来头：

Yejin Choi 曾任英伟达杰出科学家，2022 年获得被誉为「天才奖」的麦克阿瑟奖。她长期研究如何让小模型以更低成本完成复杂任务。

Carlos Guestrin 则是著名开源机器学习工具 XGBoost 的联合开发者。他创办的机器学习公司 Turi 于 2016 年被苹果收购，随后负责苹果的核心机器学习与 AI 团队。

Noeri 的起点，是斯坦福研究团队嫌 GPT-5 太贵。Choi 向彭博社透露，斯坦福一个微生物与免疫学研究团队觉得 GPT-5 太贵，于是他们训练了一个小 AI，让它学会指挥 GPT-4 等旧模型完成科研任务。结果出乎意料，这套组合在特定任务上，表现反而超过 GPT-5。

Noeri 准备沿着这个方向继续做下去。它想让企业培养自己的专用 AI，不断从实际工作中学习。比如某项工作经常出错，AI 可以分析失败原因，修改自己的工具和工作流程，必要时甚至重新训练底层模型。改动经过人工审批后再投入使用。

这个方向已经有同行在探索。日本 Sakana AI 今年 6 月就推出了 Fugu，同样训练专门的模型来指挥其他 AI，完成复杂任务。Sakana 也在研究 AI 自我改进。

Noeri 更侧重将这些能力用于企业，让 AI 长期学习企业自己的数据和工作经验，逐渐形成更便宜、更擅长特定工作的专用模型。企业也能保留自己开发的模型和工作流程。
